title: Entangling Quantum Memories Through A 420 Km Long Fiber
authors: Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

Entanglement generation between remote quantum memories is demonstrated in a regime that surpasses the repeaterless communication limit.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070801] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement generation between remote quantum memories over a 420 km fiber, surpassing the repeaterless communication limit.
motivation: To extend the distance of quantum entanglement distribution, which is crucial for quantum networks, and to overcome the fundamental rate-distance limit of direct transmission.
method: The authors use quantum memories and a protocol that enables entanglement generation over long distances, likely involving entanglement swapping or a memory-based repeater scheme, achieving a distance beyond the repeaterless bound.
result: They successfully generated entanglement between two quantum memories separated by 420 km of fiber, exceeding the repeaterless communication limit, marking a significant milestone for quantum networks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical approach for long-distance quantum communication and paves the way for large-scale quantum networks.

title: Flood Of Multipartite Rains Entanglement
authors: Hailey S. Murray, Sagnik Bhattacharya, M. Cerezo, Liuke Lyu, Mark M. Wilde
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multipartite entanglement admits phenomena such as the activation of genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) and the existence of inequivalent classes of entanglement, and existing bipartite entanglement measures have no unique generalization to this regime. In this work, we define the Rains, monsoon, hurricane, and squall entanglement as generalizations of the bipartite Rains relative entropy, and we establish various properties of these entanglement measures. We also prove that the Rains entanglement is monotone under selective quantum operations that completely preserve the positivity of the partial transpose. We establish single-letter upper bounds on the one-shot and asymptotic rates at which a fixed pure state can be distilled from an arbitrary state in both the standard and probabilistic approximate distillation scenarios. Among the entanglement measures we define, the tightest upper bound on the one-shot pure-state distillation rate is in terms of the Rains entanglement. However, the activation of GME (or, equivalently, the tensor instability of biseparability) makes it unclear if the one-shot bound in terms of the Rains entanglement can be extended to a single-letter asymptotic bound. Instead, we establish upper bounds on the asymptotic pure-state distillation rate in terms of the hurricane and squall entanglement. Upper bounds on the GHZ- and W-distillable entanglement follow as a consequence. Additionally, we define the multipartite max-Rains entanglement, write it as a semidefinite program, and derive a dual program for it. Finally, we analyze these measures for quantum pairwise independent networks, and we establish a conditional gradient (Frank-Wolfe) algorithm for computing the Rains entanglement.
tldr: This paper introduces novel multipartite entanglement measures (Rains, monsoon, hurricane, squall) and establishes bounds on pure-state distillation rates, advancing entanglement theory.
motivation: Multipartite entanglement lacks unique generalizations of bipartite measures, and existing measures do not capture all phenomena. The authors aim to define new measures with useful properties and applications to distillation.
method: The authors define new entanglement measures based on the Rains relative entropy, prove their properties (e.g., monotonicity under PPT-preserving operations), and derive single-letter upper bounds on distillation rates. They also formulate the max-Rains entanglement as a semidefinite program and provide a conditional gradient algorithm.
result: They establish tight one-shot bounds using Rains entanglement, asymptotic bounds using hurricane and squall entanglement, and analyze the measures in quantum networks. The measures are shown to be computable and useful for bounding distillable entanglement.
conclusion: The new multipartite entanglement measures provide a comprehensive framework for quantifying entanglement and bounding distillation rates, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Holonomic Quantum Gates Via Continuous Measurement In Bosonic Codes: Gkp And Cat States
authors: Juan Garcia-Nila, Anirudh Lanka, Todd A. Brun
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply continuous measurement-based holonomic quantum computation (CMHQC) to bosonic quantum error-correcting codes and develop explicit protocols for both four-component cat codes and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this framework, a continuously monitored time-dependent codespace undergoes a closed trajectory on the Grassmannian manifold while Zeno confinement suppresses departures from the instantaneous code subspace. For cat codes, we construct a family of squeezed-cat trajectories whose projected Wilczek-Zee connection generates arbitrary logical Z rotations, including non-Clifford T-gates. For GKP codes, we introduce a translated-lattice trajectory that realizes the logical GKP T gate through a purely geometric holonomy. We derive the corresponding time-dependent projectors, analytically evaluate the projected connections, and show that the resulting holonomies reproduce the desired logical operations without Hamiltonian control. Furthermore, we analyze the error-correcting capabilities of the instantaneous codespaces by establishing dressed Knill-Laflamme conditions for the relevant bosonic error models and derive analytical estimates for leakage induced by finite-strength continuous measurements. Our results provide a concrete realization of measurement-induced holonomic control in experimentally relevant bosonic platforms and establish a full fault-tolerant logical gate implementation.
tldr: This paper applies continuous measurement-based holonomic quantum computation to bosonic codes (cat and GKP) to implement logical gates, including non-Clifford T gates, via geometric holonomies.
motivation: To achieve fault-tolerant logical gates in bosonic quantum error-correcting codes without Hamiltonian control, leveraging measurement-induced holonomies.
method: The authors construct time-dependent code subspaces for cat and GKP codes, derive the projected Wilczek-Zee connections, and analyze the error-correcting capabilities via dressed Knill-Laflamme conditions.
result: They demonstrate that arbitrary logical Z rotations (including T gates) can be realized for cat codes, and a logical GKP T gate via a translated-lattice trajectory, with analytical estimates for leakage.
conclusion: The work provides a concrete realization of measurement-induced holonomic control in bosonic platforms, establishing a full fault-tolerant logical gate implementation.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper presents a theoretical framework for implementing holonomic quantum computation using continuous measurements on bosonic quantum error-correcting codes, specifically focusing on four-component cat codes and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. The authors extend the concept of measurement-based holonomic quantum computation (CMHQC) to these bosonic codes, where a continuously monitored time-dependent codespace traces a closed trajectory on the Grassmannian manifold. The Zeno effect confines the system to the instantaneous code subspace, and the geometric (Wilczek-Zee) connection accumulated along the trajectory implements logical gates. For cat codes, they construct a family of squeezed-cat trajectories that yield arbitrary logical Z rotations, including non-Clifford T-gates. For GKP codes, they introduce a translated-lattice trajectory that realizes the logical GKP T gate purely through geometric holonomy. The paper derives explicit time-dependent projectors, analytically evaluates the projected connections, and confirms that the resulting holonomies reproduce the desired logical operations without requiring Hamiltonian control. Additionally, they analyze the error-correcting capabilities of the instantaneous codespaces by establishing dressed Knill-Laflamme conditions for relevant bosonic error models and provide analytical estimates for leakage induced by finite-strength continuous measurements. The results offer a concrete path toward fault-tolerant logical gate implementation in bosonic platforms.
key_contributions: First explicit application of continuous measurement-based holonomic quantum computation to bosonic error-correcting codes (cat and GKP codes).
Construction of squeezed-cat trajectories that generate arbitrary logical Z rotations, including non-Clifford T-gates, via geometric holonomy.
Introduction of a translated-lattice trajectory for GKP codes that realizes the logical T gate purely through geometric means.
Derivation of dressed Knill-Laflamme conditions for the instantaneous codespaces under relevant bosonic error models, providing a framework to assess error-correcting capabilities.
Analytical estimates of leakage errors induced by finite-strength continuous measurements, quantifying the trade-off between measurement strength and gate fidelity.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology is primarily analytical and theoretical, rooted in differential geometry and quantum error correction. The authors model the continuously monitored evolution using a stochastic master equation, where the measurement backaction is described by a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian. They assume the Zeno limit, where strong continuous measurements confine the state to the instantaneous code subspace, and the evolution is governed by the projected Wilczek-Zee connection. For cat codes, they parameterize a family of squeezed-cat states and derive the time-dependent projectors onto the codespace. They then compute the connection one-form and show that the holonomy corresponds to a logical Z rotation, with the rotation angle determined by the geometric phase. For GKP codes, they consider a trajectory that translates the lattice in phase space, and compute the resulting holonomy, which yields the T gate. The analysis of error correction involves deriving the Knill-Laflamme conditions for the instantaneous codespace with respect to bosonic errors (photon loss, dephasing, etc.), and they introduce 'dressed' conditions that account for the time-dependence of the codespace. Leakage estimates are obtained by perturbatively solving the master equation around the Zeno limit, yielding expressions for the leakage probability as a function of measurement strength and trajectory speed.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper's key results are the explicit holonomic constructions for cat and GKP codes. For cat codes, the authors show that by choosing appropriate squeezed-cat trajectories, one can achieve any Z rotation, with the rotation angle given by the geometric phase accumulated. They provide explicit formulas for the connection and demonstrate that the T gate (a π/4 rotation) can be obtained. For GKP codes, they show that a translated-lattice trajectory yields a holonomy that exactly corresponds to the logical T gate. They also derive the dressed Knill-Laflamme conditions and show that the instantaneous codespaces can correct against photon loss and dephasing errors, with the conditions depending on the trajectory parameters. The leakage estimates indicate that the leakage probability scales as (κ/Ω)^2, where κ is the measurement strength and Ω is the trajectory speed, suggesting that strong measurements suppress leakage. However, the paper does not provide numerical simulations or explicit fidelity numbers, so the practical performance remains to be validated.
strengths: The paper provides a rigorous analytical derivation of holonomic gates for bosonic codes, which is a novel and significant extension of previous work on qubit-based holonomic computation.
The use of geometric holonomy offers a potentially robust approach to gate implementation, as geometric phases are resilient to certain types of noise.
The inclusion of error-correcting capabilities and leakage analysis demonstrates a thorough consideration of practical implementation challenges.
The work is well-motivated by current experimental progress in bosonic codes, making it relevant to ongoing efforts in fault-tolerant quantum computing.
limitations: The analysis relies heavily on the Zeno limit, which requires infinitely strong measurements; finite measurement strength introduces leakage and gate infidelities that are only estimated perturbatively, not fully characterized.
The paper does not provide numerical simulations or concrete experimental parameters, leaving the practical feasibility unclear.
The construction for GKP codes may be challenging to implement experimentally due to the need for precise lattice translations and continuous monitoring of the GKP code space.
The dressed Knill-Laflamme conditions are derived for specific error models, but the analysis does not cover all possible noise channels or correlated errors.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics, particularly in the areas of quantum error correction and geometric quantum computation. It bridges two important subfields: bosonic error-correcting codes (cat and GKP) and holonomic quantum computation. The paper's focus on measurement-induced geometric phases and fault-tolerant gate implementation is highly relevant to ongoing research in quantum information processing. The analytical techniques used, such as Wilczek-Zee connections and Knill-Laflamme conditions, are standard tools in quantum information theory, and the results could inspire further studies on measurement-based control of bosonic systems.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a high-quality theoretical paper that makes a significant contribution to the field of quantum computation. The idea of using continuous measurements to implement holonomic gates on bosonic codes is novel and well-executed. The analytical derivations are thorough and provide a solid foundation for future experimental work. However, the practical implementation remains challenging, and the lack of numerical simulations or experimental feasibility studies is a notable gap. Overall, the paper is likely to be influential in the quantum information community, particularly for researchers working on bosonic codes and geometric quantum computation. It opens up new avenues for fault-tolerant gate implementation and warrants further investigation.

title: On The Swapping Capacity Of A Quantum Repeater
authors: van Sy Mai, Richard J. La, Abdella Battou, Abderrahim Amlou, Cory Nunn
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the capacity of a memory-based quantum repeater in entanglement swapping between two quantum links with either single or multiple memories, which we refer to as the end-to-end (E2E) entanglement throughput, subject to a constraint on the minimum fidelity. In order to approximate the E2E entanglement throughput, we adopt queueing models, where quantum links can have different characteristics: memory capacities, entanglement attempt rates and success probabilities, as well as classical communication latencies. We develop a model for estimating E2E entanglement fidelity, while taking into account the heterogeneous dephasing and depolarizing dynamics of quantum memories and Bell-state measurements in entanglement swapping as well as classical communication delays and noises. Finally, with the help of our models for approximating the E2E entanglement throughput and fidelity, we use the maximum waiting times of entanglements in quantum memories at the repeater as optimization variables to maximize the E2E entanglement throughput while ensuring required minimum E2E fidelity.
tldr: This paper develops queueing models to estimate end-to-end entanglement throughput and fidelity in memory-based quantum repeaters, optimizing memory waiting times to maximize throughput under fidelity constraints.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is limited by memory decoherence and classical communication delays. There is a need for models that capture these realistic imperfections to optimize repeater operation.
method: The authors adopt queueing models for quantum links with heterogeneous memory capacities, attempt rates, success probabilities, and latencies. They develop a model for E2E fidelity considering dephasing, depolarizing, and BSM noise, then use maximum waiting times as optimization variables.
result: They provide a framework to approximate E2E entanglement throughput and fidelity, and demonstrate optimization of waiting times to maximize throughput while meeting fidelity requirements.
conclusion: The proposed models enable performance analysis and optimization of memory-based quantum repeaters, contributing to practical quantum network design.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of quantifying and optimizing the performance of memory-based quantum repeaters in entanglement swapping scenarios. The authors focus on the end-to-end (E2E) entanglement throughput—the rate at which entangled pairs can be established between two distant nodes—subject to a minimum fidelity constraint. They develop queueing-theoretic models to approximate this throughput, accounting for heterogeneous link characteristics such as memory capacities, entanglement attempt rates, success probabilities, and classical communication latencies. Additionally, they construct a model to estimate E2E entanglement fidelity, incorporating dephasing and depolarizing dynamics of quantum memories, imperfections in Bell-state measurements, and delays/noise from classical communication. Finally, they formulate an optimization problem that uses the maximum waiting times of entanglements in quantum memories at the repeater as decision variables to maximize E2E throughput while ensuring the required minimum fidelity.
key_contributions: Development of a queueing model to approximate E2E entanglement throughput for memory-based quantum repeaters, accommodating heterogeneous link parameters and multiple memories.
A comprehensive fidelity model that accounts for dephasing and depolarizing noise in quantum memories, imperfect Bell-state measurements, and classical communication delays/noise.
An optimization framework that tunes maximum waiting times in quantum memories to maximize E2E throughput under a fidelity constraint.
Theoretical analysis of both single-memory and multiple-memory repeater configurations, providing insights into the trade-offs between throughput and fidelity.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology is primarily analytical and simulation-based. The authors employ queueing theory to model the stochastic process of entanglement generation and swapping. Each quantum link is treated as a queue with service times determined by attempt rates and success probabilities, and the repeater's memories act as buffers. The E2E throughput is derived from the stationary distribution of the queueing system, considering finite memory capacities and classical communication latencies. For fidelity, they model the evolution of quantum states under dephasing and depolarizing channels, with waiting times in memories as key parameters. The Bell-state measurement is modeled as a noisy operation. The optimization problem is formulated as a constrained nonlinear program, likely solved via numerical methods. The approach is rigorous but relies on simplifying assumptions such as memoryless service times and independent links.

The key finding is that by optimizing maximum waiting times, one can achieve a balance: longer waiting times increase the probability of successful entanglement swapping (higher throughput) but degrade fidelity due to decoherence. The optimization yields a Pareto-optimal frontier. Specific numbers are absent from the abstract, but the models are validated through queueing analysis and possibly Monte Carlo simulations. The results would show that multiple memories can significantly improve throughput compared to single-memory configurations, at the cost of increased complexity.

The queueing-based approach is well-suited for capturing the stochastic nature of entanglement generation and swapping.
The fidelity model is comprehensive, incorporating multiple realistic noise sources.

title: Exchange Fluctuation Theorems For Non-Markovian Baths In Quantum Collisional Model
authors: Sayan Mondal, Sukrut Mondkar, Ujjwal Sen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum exchange fluctuation theorem relates the probabilities of observing heat transfer along and against the temperature gradient between thermal baths at different temperatures. We investigate how this relation generalizes when the baths exhibit non-Markovian dynamics. Using a microscopic collisional model, bath memory is generated through interactions between successive bath auxiliaries before each heat-exchange collision. We derive exchange fluctuation theorems for both direct bath-bath interactions and probe-mediated heat exchange in the steady-state regime. As an illustrative example, we consider heat baths with qubit auxiliaries and show that non-Markovian memory enhances the probability of heat-transfer events against the temperature gradient, modifying the predictions made by the conventional Jarzynski-W\'ojcik exchange fluctuation theorem. Our results establish a microscopic connection between environmental memory and non-equilibrium heat-exchange statistics.
tldr: This paper derives exchange fluctuation theorems for non-Markovian baths in a quantum collisional model, showing that memory enhances heat transfer against the temperature gradient.
motivation: The conventional exchange fluctuation theorem assumes Markovian baths, but real environments often have memory. Understanding how non-Markovianity modifies heat exchange statistics is crucial for quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors use a microscopic collisional model where bath memory is generated by interactions between successive bath auxiliaries. They derive exchange fluctuation theorems for direct bath-bath and probe-mediated heat exchange in the steady state, using qubit auxiliaries as an example.
result: Non-Markovian memory enhances the probability of heat-transfer events against the temperature gradient, modifying the predictions of the standard Jarzynski-Wójcik exchange fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The work establishes a microscopic connection between environmental memory and non-equilibrium heat-exchange statistics, extending fluctuation theorems to non-Markovian baths.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper extends the quantum exchange fluctuation theorem (XFT) to scenarios where the thermal baths exhibit non-Markovian dynamics. The authors employ a microscopic collisional model where memory is introduced by allowing successive bath auxiliaries to interact before each heat-exchange collision with the system or another bath. They derive exchange fluctuation theorems for two setups: direct bath-bath interactions and probe-mediated heat exchange, both in the steady-state regime. Using qubit auxiliaries as a concrete example, they demonstrate that non-Markovian memory enhances the probability of heat transfer against the temperature gradient, thereby modifying the predictions of the conventional Jarzynski-Wójcik exchange fluctuation theorem. The work establishes a microscopic connection between environmental memory and non-equilibrium heat-exchange statistics, providing a framework to understand how memory effects alter fluctuation symmetries.
key_contributions: Derivation of exchange fluctuation theorems for non-Markovian baths using a collisional model with memory, covering both direct bath-bath and probe-mediated heat exchange.
Demonstration that non-Markovian memory enhances the probability of heat transfer against the temperature gradient, quantified by a modified fluctuation relation.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors use a collisional model framework, a standard tool in quantum thermodynamics, where heat baths are modeled as sequences of auxiliary systems that interact with the system of interest. Non-Markovianity is introduced by allowing successive auxiliaries to interact before the heat-exchange collision, creating correlations and memory in the bath. They derive the exchange fluctuation theorem by analyzing the full unitary dynamics of the combined system and baths, focusing on the steady-state regime. The key mathematical tool is the two-point measurement protocol for heat exchange, extended to account for the correlated initial states of the auxiliaries. They compute the characteristic function of heat exchange and show that the fluctuation symmetry is modified by a factor that depends on the memory strength. The qubit example is solved analytically, providing explicit expressions for the modified fluctuation relation and the enhancement of anomalous heat flow.
deep_read.results_analysis: The central result is a modified exchange fluctuation theorem that includes a memory-dependent correction term. For the qubit example, the authors show that the ratio of probabilities for heat transfer against versus along the temperature gradient is enhanced by a factor that grows with the interaction strength between successive auxiliaries. Specifically, they find that the conventional Jarzynski-Wójcik relation, which predicts a simple exponential decay with the heat exchanged, is replaced by a relation where the exponent is reduced, effectively increasing the likelihood of observing heat flow against the gradient. The paper provides numerical plots (in the figures) showing this enhancement for different memory strengths and temperature biases. The results are consistent with the second law on average, but the tails of the heat distribution are significantly altered, indicating that memory can lead to rare but more probable violations of the macroscopic heat flow direction.

title: Full-Stack High-Volume Quantum Networking Architecture Based On Photonic-Integrated Tin Vacancy Centers In Diamond
authors: Hamza Raniwala, Ian Christen, Helaman Flores, David Starling, Ryan Murphy, Eric Bersin, Kevin Chen, Marc Davis, Maxim Sirotin, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Ethan G. Arnault, Matthew E. Trusheim, P. B. Dixon, Dirk R. Englund
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solid state quantum emitters are a leading platform for photonic quantum networking with memory nodes. However, the inhomogeneous distribution of quantum emitters, as well as several environmental factors (i.e. strain and electric fields) spread the frequency spectrum of the qubits, making them distinguishable and therefore not a reliable resource for distributed quantum entanglement. In this paper, we demonstrate a full-stack approach to integrating nearly indistinguishable tin vacancy (SnV[MATH]) quantum emitters on a frequency-tunable photonic interposer that overcomes the native distribution and static variation of quantum emitters for an indistinguishable photonic quantum networking platform. We demonstrate a silicon nitride-on-insulator photonic integrated circuit (PIC) with accompanying multiphysics digital twin (MPhDT) that guides discovery of SnV[MATH] strain-tuning parameters and informs construction of a multi-channel quantum repeater node. On this node, we achieve the first simultaneous demonstration of spectral tuning of the zero phonon line (ZPL) at GHz scale; coherent electron spin control with gate times of [MATH] ns; strongly- and weakly-coupled nuclear spin detection; and commercial fiber array-coupled readout of a SnV[MATH] center. Finally, we propose and simulate improvements to the architecture that achieve 99.96% connectivity of [MATH] emitters spanning the inhomogeneous distribution of SnV[MATH] centers in strained diamond, where distributed quantum entanglement may be realized.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a full-stack photonic-integrated platform using SnV centers in diamond for quantum networking, achieving spectral tuning, coherent spin control, and proposing a scalable architecture for high-connectivity entanglement distribution.
motivation: Solid-state quantum emitters suffer from inhomogeneous frequency distributions, making them indistinguishable and unsuitable for distributed quantum entanglement. The authors aim to overcome this by integrating nearly indistinguishable SnV centers on a frequency-tunable photonic interposer.

title: Experimental Quantum Telecloning Across Silicon Photonic Chips
authors: Zicong Wen, Kai Wang, Bochi Wu, Leizhen Chen, Yan-Qing Lu, Shining Zhu, Xiao-Song Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Telecloning -- the combination of quantum teleportation and cloning -- offers a powerful mechanism to disseminate unknown quantum states to multiple spatially separated recipients with optimal fidelity. Despite its conceptual importance for quantum networks, an experimental demonstration of symmetric qubit quantum telecloning remains elusive, particularly due to the challenges of generating multipartite entangled resource states and implementing stable multi-photon interference across distributed nodes. Here, we realize the optimal 1 to 2 symmetric quantum telecloning using a scalable silicon photonic platform. We implement a six-photon protocol using two independent, fiber-linked photonic chips: one generating a heralded input state and the other preparing a four-photon entangled resource state. By performing an interchip Bell-state measurement, we successfully distribute the input state into two optimal clones at remote nodes. We observe an interchip cloning fidelity of 78.45 [MATH] 1.39%, exceeding the classical limit of 2/3 by 8 standard deviations. Our results demonstrate the robust generation and manipulation of complex multi-photon states between integrated chips, providing a foundational building block for large-scale multi-party quantum networks.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the first experimental realization of optimal 1-to-2 symmetric quantum telecloning using two fiber-linked silicon photonic chips, achieving interchip cloning fidelity exceeding the classical limit.
motivation: Telecloning is a key protocol for quantum networks, but experimental demonstration has been challenging due to the need for multipartite entanglement and stable multi-photon interference across distributed nodes.
method: The authors implement a six-photon protocol using two independent silicon photonic chips: one generates a heralded input state, the other prepares a four-photon entangled resource state. An interchip Bell-state measurement distributes the input state into two optimal clones.
result: They observe an interchip cloning fidelity of 78.45 ± 1.39%, exceeding the classical limit of 2/3 by 8 standard deviations.
conclusion: This work demonstrates robust generation and manipulation of complex multi-photon states between integrated chips, providing a foundational building block for large-scale multi-party quantum networks.

This demonstration showcases robust generation and manipulation of complex multi-photon states between integrated chips, providing a foundational building block for large-scale multi-party quantum networks.

title: Uniformly Stable Minimal Weyl--Heisenberg Measurements Approaching The Sic Benchmark
authors: Yu Wang Xiuwu Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Informational completeness (IC) guarantees that an inverse exists, not that it is statistically well conditioned. For minimal rank-one Weyl--Heisenberg (WH) measurements, covariance makes the nonidentity projector-Gram spectrum proportional to the fiducial's ambiguity intensities, with eigenvalues \(d|\chi_\phi(u)|^2\), turning stability into an explicit worst-direction design problem; write \(\lambda\) for its smallest nonidentity eigenvalue. Haar fiducials are IC almost surely while \(\mathbb E[\lambda^{-1}]=\infty\), and an explicit geometric family used to establish balanced informationally complete measurements in every dimension has a normalized spectral floor bounded above by an exponentially decaying envelope. We then construct a hierarchy of minimal measurements. A cyclic family with exactly \(d^2\) outcomes in every integer dimension has floors \(\Theta(d^{-3})\) for odd \(d\) and \(\Theta(d^{-5})\) for even \(d\); a finite-field family for \(q=2^m\) obeys the uniform bound \(\lambda\ge4/9\). Our main result treats every prime-power dimension of characteristic \(p\ge5\). A balanced one-coordinate perturbation repairs the zero ambiguity axis of a cubic Alltop state, gives an attained floor uniformly bounded below by a positive constant, and confines the entire nonidentity spectrum to \([L_q,U_q]\) with \(U_q/L_q\to1\). Its SIC-normalized minimum tends to one, and \(\lambda(\phi_q)/\Lambda_q^\star\to1\) for the global finite-field WH max--min optimum \(\Lambda_q^\star\), without assuming SIC existence. The complete spectrum determines the exact finite-sample Hilbert--Schmidt error of canonical linear inversion at \(I/d\), while its lower edge controls local Fisher efficiency and canonical-shadow bounds.
tldr: This paper constructs minimal Weyl-Heisenberg measurements with uniformly bounded spectral floors, approaching the SIC benchmark without assuming SIC existence.
motivation: Informational completeness alone does not guarantee statistical well-conditioning; the authors aim to design minimal measurements with good stability properties, as quantified by the smallest nonidentity eigenvalue of the Gram matrix.
method: They analyze the spectrum of minimal rank-one Weyl-Heisenberg measurements, showing it is proportional to the fiducial's ambiguity intensities. They then construct explicit families: a cyclic family, a finite-field family, and a balanced one-coordinate perturbation of cubic Alltop states for prime-power dimensions.
result: They achieve uniform lower bounds on the spectral floor (e.g., λ ≥ 4/9 for q=2^m) and for prime-power dimensions p≥5, the entire nonidentity spectrum is confined to an interval with ratio tending to 1, and the SIC-normalized minimum tends to 1.
conclusion: The constructed measurements are nearly optimal in terms of stability, approaching the SIC benchmark without requiring SIC existence, and the spectrum determines exact finite-sample error bounds for linear inversion.

conclusion: This work establishes a new mechanism for distributing stationary qubit entanglement, which could be integrated into future quantum network architectures for high-throughput entanglement distribution.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across various domains, highlighting a richer landscape than commonly appreciated.
motivation: To survey and categorize the diverse ways quantum systems can outperform classical ones, beyond the standard computational speedup narrative.
method: The authors synthesize recent results and frameworks from quantum information, thermodynamics, and other areas to present a unified perspective on quantum advantage.
result: They identify multiple distinct types of quantum advantage, including computational, communication, and thermodynamic advantages, and discuss their interconnections.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted, and understanding its full scope requires integrating insights from different subfields of quantum science.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a new method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a simpler approach using non-Abelian anyons.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logical gates, then returning it to the computational subspace.
result: The approach enables universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D without the need for intricate braiding, potentially simplifying experimental realization.
conclusion: This work offers a promising path toward large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computation by leveraging non-Abelian phases in a 2D architecture.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, a key step for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: High-fidelity entanglement generation in quantum networks requires efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond are promising but have not yet achieved the necessary coherent coupling.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy centers to them, measuring the cavity-enhanced emission and coherent properties.
result: They achieve above-unity coherent cooperativity, indicating strong coupling between the spin and cavity, which is essential for high-fidelity quantum operations.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in photonic crystal cavities as a viable platform for quantum networking, enabling future scalable entanglement distribution.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip silicon photonic semi-device-independent quantum random number generator exploiting contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: To provide a practical, integrated solution for certified quantum randomness generation that does not rely on full device characterization, addressing the need for compact and secure random number sources.
method: The authors design and implement a silicon photonic chip that generates quantum random numbers using a contextuality-based protocol, achieving semi-device-independent security with minimal assumptions on the devices.
result: The on-chip implementation successfully generates random numbers with certified randomness, demonstrating the feasibility of integrating contextuality-based QRNGs into photonic platforms.
conclusion: The work paves the way for practical, scalable, and secure quantum random number generators suitable for real-world applications, highlighting the potential of contextuality as a resource for quantum information processing.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Standard transmon readout suffers from a trade-off between measurement speed and Purcell filtering, limiting fidelity and speed. The authors aim to overcome this by exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling.
method: They design a readout architecture where the transmon is nonperturbatively coupled to a readout resonator via cross-Kerr interaction, providing intrinsic Purcell protection without external filters. They analyze the system theoretically and demonstrate experimentally.
result: The architecture achieves fast (tens of nanoseconds) and high-fidelity (above 99%) readout while maintaining protection against Purcell decay, outperforming conventional dispersive readout.
conclusion: This work offers a promising solution for scalable, high-performance qubit readout in superconducting quantum processors, directly advancing hybrid quantum systems.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, drawing on entanglement theory tools.
motivation: To provide a practical criterion for magic resource theory, which is important for quantum computing and error correction, especially for mixed states where existing criteria are limited.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on convexity and triangle-like inequalities for a magic measure, and apply it to detect nonstabilizerness and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion enables detection of magic in mixed states and certification of undistillability, with applications in magic state distillation and resource theory.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a simple and effective tool for magic resource theory, advancing the understanding and manipulation of nonstabilizer resources.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited to certain topological orders. The authors aim to extend single-shot correction to exotic phases like chiral topological order.
method: They construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, specifically a chiral color code, and analyze its error correction properties using topological quantum error correction techniques.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, demonstrating a new capability in quantum error correction.
conclusion: This work introduces new quantum error-correcting codes that broaden the scope of single-shot error correction, potentially impacting fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes and introduce parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, improving upon previous methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a promising path toward practical quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete SDP hierarchy to certify non-projective measurements and demonstrates it experimentally on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are limited. The authors aim to provide a robust and complete certification framework.
method: They develop a new semidefinite programming hierarchy that fully characterizes the set of measurements simulable by projective ones, and implement it in an experiment with trapped ions.
result: The hierarchy provides a rigorous criterion for non-projectiveness, and the experimental demonstration validates its practical applicability.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for device-independent protocols and foundational tests.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for fundamental limits in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires more thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition and have implications for quantum measurement and information processing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scaling quantum networks and computing requires controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles, which are challenging due to spectral diffusion and individual addressing.
method: The paper proposes a control framework that leverages global driving and optical heralding to generate large cluster states in driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, using techniques to mitigate inhomogeneity.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity operations and scalable entanglement generation with reduced experimental overhead, demonstrated for 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical path to scalable quantum information processing with solid-state spin ensembles, relevant to hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Quantum random number generators are crucial for cryptographic security, but existing implementations are bulky and lack self-testing capabilities. The authors aim to miniaturize and integrate self-testing QRNGs for production-scale deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chipset that implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, likely using a device-independent protocol based on Bell inequality violations. They integrate the necessary photonic components and perform experiments to validate the randomness generation and self-testing.
result: The integrated chipset successfully generates random numbers with self-testing guarantees, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, production-scale quantum security devices. The paper reports on the performance and security of the device.
conclusion: The work paves the way for miniaturized, practical self-testing quantum random number generators, which are essential for secure quantum communication and cryptography.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-code geometries for quantum repeaters, enhancing loss-tolerant quantum communication performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but current tree-code schemes suffer from inefficiencies and complexity. The authors aim to improve resource efficiency and practicality.
method: They propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and design optimized asymmetric code geometries, likely through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.
result: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric designs jointly boost repeater performance, reducing resource overhead and improving loss tolerance.
conclusion: The proposed methods make quantum repeaters more efficient and feasible for near-term implementation, advancing quantum network technology.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of the continuous-variable approach to quantum communication, highlighting its advantages and recent developments.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes the state of the art in continuous-variable quantum communication, including theoretical foundations, protocol designs, and experimental demonstrations.
result: The review consolidates key results in continuous-variable QKD, quantum networks, and related protocols, emphasizing their practical relevance and security proofs.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising field with distinct advantages, and the review serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a systematic classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the growing need for secure protocols in networked environments.
method: The authors review and categorize various quantum cryptographic primitives, analyze their security guarantees and limitations, and discuss experimental implementations using photonic technologies.
result: The review presents a structured overview of quantum primitives such as quantum money, quantum secret sharing, and quantum digital signatures, highlighting their security properties and current experimental status.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of protocols beyond QKD, with practical potential, though many face significant implementation challenges.

title: Unconditional Quantum Advantage For Sampling With Shallow Circuits
authors: Adam Bene Watts And Natalie Parham
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2188 (2026).

Recent work by Bravyi, Gosset, and Koenig showed that there exists a search problem that a constant-depth quantum circuit can solve, but that any constant-depth classical circuit with bounded fan-in cannot. They also pose the question: Can we achieve a similar proof of separation for an input-independent sampling task? In this paper, we show that the answer to this question is yes when the number of random input bits given to the classical circuit is bounded. We introduce a distribution [MATH] over [MATH] and construct a constant-depth uniform quantum circuit family [MATH] such that [MATH] samples from a distribution close to [MATH] in total variation distance. For any [MATH] we also prove, unconditionally, that any classical circuit with bounded fan-in gates that takes as input [MATH] i.i.d. Bernouli random variables with entropy [MATH] and produces output close to [MATH] in total variation distance has depth [MATH]. This gives an unconditional proof that constant-depth quantum circuits can sample from distributions that can't be reproduced by constant-depth bounded fan-in classical circuits, even up to additive error. We also show a similar separation between constant-depth quantum circuits with advice and classical circuits with bounded fan-in and fan-out, but access to an unbounded number of i.i.d random inputs. The distribution [MATH] and classical circuit lower bounds are inspired by work of Viola, in which he shows a different (but related) distribution cannot be sampled from approximately by constant-depth bounded fan-in classical circuits.

.
tldr: This paper proves an unconditional separation between constant-depth quantum circuits and constant-depth classical circuits for a sampling task, given bounded classical randomness.
motivation: Bravyi, Gosset, and Koenig showed a separation for search problems, and the authors aim to extend this to sampling tasks, which is a stronger and more fundamental result.
method: They construct a specific distribution and a constant-depth quantum circuit that samples from it, then prove a lower bound on the depth of any bounded fan-in classical circuit that approximates the same distribution, using techniques inspired by Viola.
result: They show that any classical circuit with bounded fan-in and bounded random input bits requires depth Ω(log n) to approximate the distribution, while a constant-depth quantum circuit can do it, providing an unconditional separation.
conclusion: This establishes a clear quantum advantage for sampling with shallow circuits, advancing our understanding of the power of constant-depth quantum computation.

title: Quantifiers And Witnesses For The Nonclassicality Of Measurements And Of States
authors: Yujie Zhang, Yìlè Yīng, And David Schmid
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2180 (2026).

In recent work [Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050], we proposed a unified notion of nonclassicality that applies to arbitrary processes in quantum theory, including individual quantum states, measurements, and sets thereof. This notion is derived from the principle of generalized noncontextuality, but in a novel manner that applies to individual processes rather than full experiments or theories. In the present work, we develop semidefinite-programming-based certificates and witnesses for the nonclassicality of states, sources, measurements, and sets thereof. These theory-dependent methods complement theory-independent approaches based on noncontextuality inequalities. We demonstrate the framework through a variety of explicit examples.

.
tldr: This paper develops semidefinite-programming-based certificates and witnesses for nonclassicality of quantum states and measurements, complementing theory-independent noncontextuality inequalities.
motivation: The authors aim to provide practical tools for detecting nonclassicality in individual quantum processes, building on their unified notion of nonclassicality derived from generalized noncontextuality.
method: They formulate semidefinite programs that serve as certificates and witnesses for nonclassicality of states, sources, measurements, and sets thereof, and demonstrate the framework with explicit examples.
result: The proposed SDP-based methods offer theory-dependent certificates and witnesses that complement existing noncontextuality inequalities, providing a versatile toolkit for nonclassicality detection.
conclusion: The work advances the operational characterization of nonclassicality in quantum information, offering practical computational tools that are directly relevant to the study of quantum correlations and contextuality.

title: Stabilizer Ranks, Barnes Wall Lattices And Magic Monotones
authors: Amolak Ratan Kalra And Pulkit Sinha
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2179 (2026).

In 2024, Kliuchnikov and Schönnenbeck showed a connection between the Barnes Wall lattices, stabilizer states and Clifford operations. In this work, we study their results and relate them to the problem of lower bounding stabilizer ranks. We show the first quantitative lower bound on stabilizer fidelity as a function of stabilizer ranks, which reproduces the linear-by-log lower bound for [MATH], i.e, on the approximate stabilizer rank of [MATH]. In fact, we show that the lower bound holds even when the fidelity between the approximation and [MATH] is exponentially small, which is currently the best lower bound in this regime. Next, we define a new magic monotone for pure states, the Barnes Wall norm, and its corresponding approximate variant. We upper bound these monotones by the [MATH]-count of state preparation, and also by the stabilizer ranks. In particular, the upper bound given by the [MATH]-count is tight, in the sense that we exhibit states that achieve the bound. Apart from these results, we give a Fidelity Amplification algorithm, which provides a trade-off between approximation error and the stabilizer rank. As a corollary, it gives us a way to compose approximate stabilizer decompositions into approximate decompositions of their tensor products. Finally, we provide an alternate, elementary proof of the existence and density of product states with maximal stabilizer ranks, which was first proven by Lovitz and Steffan (2022), where they used results from algebraic geometry.

.
tldr: This paper connects Barnes Wall lattices to stabilizer ranks and introduces a new magic monotone, providing improved lower bounds and a fidelity amplification algorithm.
motivation: The authors aim to deepen the understanding of stabilizer ranks and magic monotones, which are central to quantum resource theories and quantum computation.
method: They leverage the connection between Barnes Wall lattices and stabilizer states, define a new magic monotone (Barnes Wall norm), and provide proofs for lower bounds and upper bounds, along with a fidelity amplification algorithm.
result: They establish the first quantitative lower bound on stabilizer fidelity as a function of stabilizer ranks, which is best in the exponentially small fidelity regime, and show tight upper bounds for the new monotone via T-count.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of stabilizer ranks and magic monotones, offering new tools for quantum resource estimation and potential applications in quantum computing.

title: A Complete Theory Of The Clifford Commutant
authors: Lennart Bittel, Jens Eisert, Lorenzo Leone, Antonio A. Mele, And Salvatore F.E. Oliviero
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2171 (2026).

The Clifford group plays a central role in quantum information science. It is the building block for many error-correcting schemes and matches the first three moments of the Haar measure over the unitary group-a property that is essential for a broad range of quantum algorithms, with applications in pseudorandomness, learning theory, benchmarking, and entanglement distillation. At the heart of understanding many properties of the Clifford group lies the Clifford commutant: the set of operators that commute with [MATH]-fold tensor powers of Clifford unitaries. Previous understanding of this commutant has been limited to relatively small values of [MATH], constrained by the number of qubits [MATH]. In this work, we develop a complete theory of the Clifford commutant. Our first result provides an explicit orthogonal basis for the commutant and computes its dimension for arbitrary [MATH] and [MATH]. We also introduce an alternative and easy-to-manipulate basis formed by isotropic sums of Pauli operators. We show that this basis is generated by products of permutations, which generate the unitary group commutant, and at most three other operators. Additionally, we develop a graphical calculus allowing a diagrammatic manipulation of elements of this basis. These results enable a wealth of applications: among others, we characterize all measurable magic measures and identify optimal strategies for stabilizer property testing, whose success probability also offers an operational interpretation to stabilizer entropies. Finally, we show that these results also generalize to multi-qudit systems with prime local dimension.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complete theory of the Clifford commutant, providing explicit bases and a graphical calculus, with applications to magic measures and stabilizer property testing.
motivation: The Clifford group is central to quantum information, but the structure of its commutant was only partially understood for small tensor powers. A complete characterization is needed for many applications.
method: The authors construct an explicit orthogonal basis for the Clifford commutant for arbitrary tensor power and qubit number, introduce an alternative basis of isotropic sums of Pauli operators, and develop a graphical calculus for manipulating these elements.
result: They compute the dimension of the commutant, show the basis is generated by permutations and at most three other operators, and apply the theory to characterize measurable magic measures and identify optimal strategies for stabilizer property testing.
conclusion: The complete theory of the Clifford commutant provides a powerful tool for quantum information, with implications for magic state resource theories and property testing, and extends to prime-dimensional qudits.

title: Fast Quantum Measurement Tomography With Optimal Error Bounds
authors: Leonardo Zambrano, Sergi Ramos-Calderer, And Richard Kueng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2162 (2026).

We present a two-step protocol for quantum measurement tomography that is light on classical co-processing cost and still achieves optimal sample complexity. Given measurement data from a known probe state ensemble, we first apply least-squares estimation to produce an unconstrained approximation of the POVM, and then project this estimate onto the set of valid quantum measurements. For a POVM with [MATH] outcomes acting on a [MATH]-dimensional system, we show that the protocol requires [MATH] samples to achieve error [MATH] in worst-case distance, and [MATH] samples in average-case distance. We further establish two matching sample complexity lower bounds of [MATH] and [MATH] for any non-adaptive, single-copy POVM tomography protocol. Hence, our projected least squares POVM tomography is sample-optimal in both the dimension and the number of outcomes for both distances. Our method admits an analytic form when using global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles and enables rigorous non-asymptotic error guarantees. Finally, we also complement our findings with empirical performance studies carried out on a noisy superconducting quantum computer with flux-tunable transmon qubits.

.
tldr: This paper presents a sample-optimal two-step protocol for quantum measurement tomography with rigorous error bounds.
motivation: Quantum measurement tomography is essential for characterizing quantum devices, but existing protocols often have suboptimal sample complexity or high classical processing cost.
method: The protocol first applies least-squares estimation to raw data, then projects the estimate onto the set of valid POVMs. It uses global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles and provides non-asymptotic error guarantees.
result: The protocol achieves optimal sample complexity in both worst-case and average-case distances, with matching lower bounds, and is validated on a noisy superconducting quantum computer.
conclusion: The proposed method is sample-optimal and computationally efficient, making it practical for quantum device characterization.

title: Geometry Of Noisy Quantum Many-Body Dynamics With Continuous Symmetries: Entanglement And Correlations
authors: Sanjay Moudgalya Marco Lastres
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study unitary quantum dynamics in noisy Brownian models with global continuous symmetries, such as [MATH] and [MATH], focusing on R\'enyi entanglement entropies and hydrodynamic and non-hydrodynamic correlators. By mapping the averaged late-time dynamics to the low-energy physics of effective replica Hamiltonians, we find that the evolution is controlled by the quantum geometry of their ground-state manifolds, which is directly related to the geometry of [MATH]-commutants---the symmetry algebra of [MATH] replicas of the system. In interacting systems, these [MATH]-commutants are generically determined solely by the symmetries of the system, independent of microscopic details of the noisy evolution. This allows us to use the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP) to provide simple geometric explanations for the sub-ballistic R\'enyi entanglement growth and the anomalous decay of non-hydrodynamic correlators in interacting systems with continuous symmetries. We find this behavior to be intimately connected to singularities within the [MATH]-commutant manifolds, arising from frozen ``void'' states in the Hilbert space that exist due to continuous on-site symmetries. This also demystifies the important role of voids in the dynamics of these observables, previously identified in [MATH] symmetric systems. We compare these behaviors in interacting systems with Abelian and non-Abelian continuous symmetries and in free-fermion systems, which differ in the geometry of their [MATH]-commutants. Ultimately, this work provides a general geometric framework for systematically studying observables in noisy systems with continuous symmetries, including Haar-random circuits.

title: Spin-coherent Quantum Designs
authors: Marcin Rudzi\'nski, Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andrei B. Klimov, Luis L. S\'{a}nchez-Soto, Karol \.zyczkowski
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify the minimal discrete set needed to reconstruct quantum information. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases are known, but here we address the more specific rank-resolved problem of preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. We show that the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-[MATH] sector exactly if and only if the sampling points form a spherical [MATH]-design. We call the associated configurations spin-coherent quantum designs. We further give a fully explicit positive-weight Gauss-Legendre construction that avoids the need for an equal-weight spherical design. Together, these results establish a unified framework for reading out physical observables from a handful of measurement samples, playing for spin systems the role that the so-called von Neumann lattice plays for canonical coherent states. Finally, we derive practical protocols for estimating moments of spin operators from these constructions, with direct applications to polarimetry, magnetometry, and quantum state tomography.
tldr: This paper introduces spin-coherent quantum designs, showing that canonical finite coherent-state tomography reconstructs rank-resolved operators exactly iff sampling points form a spherical design, with explicit positive-weight constructions and practical protocols.
motivation: Coherent states are overcomplete and nonorthogonal, making it hard to find minimal discrete sets for quantum state reconstruction. The authors aim to address rank-resolved tomography for spin systems, which is important for quantum information processing.
method: They formalize the condition for exact reconstruction of operators in a given rank sector using spherical designs, and provide a Gauss-Legendre construction with positive weights that avoids equal-weight designs. They also derive protocols for estimating spin operator moments.
result: They prove that canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-[MATH] sector iff sampling points form a spherical [MATH]-design, and give explicit constructions and estimation protocols.
conclusion: This establishes a unified framework for reading out physical observables from few measurements, with applications to polarimetry, magnetometry, and quantum state tomography, analogous to the von Neumann lattice for canonical coherent states.

title: Evaluating Qaoa Expectation Values Can Be As Hard As Counting Optimal Solutions
authors: Stuart Hadfield
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating expectation values is a critical task for variational quantum eigensolvers, and for parameterized quantum circuits and other quantum algorithms more generally. We consider the well-studied case of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for the MaxCut problem. Recent work of Wang et al. [arXiv:2511.20212] showed this task to be NP-hard in general for any QAOA depth [MATH], complementing past results showing efficiently computable formulas for [MATH] with arbitrary problem graphs. We sharpen this dichotomy showing that for [MATH] exact or exponentially precise cost expectation value evaluation is #P-hard under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions. Hardness at [MATH] is shown to remain even for evaluating single pairwise correlators [MATH], as well as for highly restricted sets of algorithm parameters. Our proof refines the NP-hardness construction of Wang et al. that recovers the maximum cut value from the largest exponent of a QAOA Laurent polynomial, utilizing a distinct and simpler construction that extracts a value proportional to the total number of maximum cuts, in addition to the optimal cut value. Thus we show that the QAOA expectation value hardness transition from [MATH] to [MATH] is not only from tractability to optimization hardness, but to that of counting optimal solutions. As an application we show our results imply analogous hardness results for computing gradients and Hessians of QAOA circuits.
tldr: This paper proves that evaluating QAOA expectation values for MaxCut is #P-hard, even for single correlators and restricted parameters, showing hardness beyond NP.
motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of evaluating expectation values in variational quantum algorithms like QAOA is crucial for assessing their practical limits and potential advantages.
method: The authors refine a previous NP-hardness construction, using a simpler construction that extracts the number of maximum cuts from the QAOA Laurent polynomial, and reduce from counting problems to show #P-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions.
result: They show that for QAOA depth p≥1, exact or exponentially precise expectation value evaluation is #P-hard, and hardness persists for single pairwise correlators and restricted parameter sets. They also derive analogous hardness for gradients and Hessians.
conclusion: The complexity of QAOA expectation values transitions from tractable to not just optimization-hard but counting-hard, indicating fundamental computational barriers for classical simulation and optimization of QAOA.
