method: The paper reviews recent work applying maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to data from simultaneous recordings of thousands of neurons.
result: The review highlights new reproducible behaviors and argues that abstract theoretical principles can achieve predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for understanding collective neural dynamics, with potential for deeper insights into brain function.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on photophysical processes.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical models for internal conversion and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper is a review that surveys various theoretical approaches to describe nonradiative transitions in quantum systems.
result: Summarizes the state of the art in modeling internal conversion and discusses potential applications.
conclusion: The review highlights the importance of these models for advancing photonics and energy harvesting technologies.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To provide an overview of quantum properties of magnetic skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics and quantum technologies.
method: The paper is a review article (Colloquium) that synthesizes existing theoretical and experimental results on quantum aspects of skyrmions, including interactions and quantum behavior.
result: It summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmion systems, such as quantum fluctuations and potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: The review highlights open questions and future directions for exploiting quantum properties of skyrmions, but does not present new research findings.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, potentially mediated by new bosons and related to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To summarize the state of the art in searches for new spin-dependent forces, which could reveal physics beyond the Standard Model and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review that compiles theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent exotic interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them, including precision measurements with atomic, molecular, and solid-state systems.
result: The review catalogs numerous experimental constraints on various exotic spin-dependent interactions and discusses future prospects for improved sensitivity.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, and ongoing and future experiments may uncover evidence for such interactions.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Stellar nuclear reactions are crucial for element formation but are difficult to measure directly at low energies, motivating theoretical advances.
method: The paper reviews the state-of-the-art theoretical approaches for low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum-mechanical models and new experimental ideas.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical methods and highlights new strategies for studying stellar reactions on Earth.
conclusion: The review underscores the importance of quantum effects in stellar nucleosynthesis and suggests future directions for research.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to violate classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that the violations arise from violating assumptions in the bounds' derivations.
motivation: To clarify why some measured material properties exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how designing materials to violate these assumptions can lead to interesting properties.
method: The paper is a review (Colloquium) that surveys various circumstances where thermodynamic bounds are exceeded, categorizing the violated assumptions and discussing how materials can be designed accordingly.
result: It identifies multiple cases where measurements exceed bounds due to assumptions like equilibrium, homogeneity, or linearity being violated, and demonstrates how this can be exploited for material design.
conclusion: The apparent violations are not actual violations of thermodynamics but result from misapplying the bounds; understanding this allows for the development of materials with enhanced properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, with applications to simulating topological phenomena and models of gravity.
motivation: To provide an overview of recent advances in realizing exotic geometries for quantum many-body systems, which could enable simulations of phenomena beyond standard Euclidean lattices.
method: The paper is a review (Colloquium) that synthesizes results from atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, discussing theoretical concepts and experimental platforms for implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher-dimensional synthetic dimensions.
result: The review highlights various platforms and techniques for creating synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries, and discusses potential applications in simulating topological phases and gravitational models.
conclusion: The field is rapidly developing, offering new opportunities for quantum simulation, but the paper does not present novel technical results directly aligned with the user's specific research directions.

title: Excitons In 2H-MoTe2: Anisotropies, Masses And Binding Energy
authors: Zahra Ahmadi Heidari And Martin Knupfer
abstract: Bound electron–hole pairs called excitons determine the photophysical behavior of semiconducting materials. In this study, we present a combination of electron energy-loss spectroscopy in transmission and optical absorption spectroscopy for the investigation of excitons in bulk 2H-MoTe2. The exciton dispersion E(q) was measured for momentum transfers oriented along the ΓK and ΓM directions at 20 K. From the extracted dispersion relations, the in-plane exciton effective mass was determined. Our results reveal that for 2H-MoTe2 the exciton effective mass is anisotropic. In consideration of the complementary optical results the exciton reduced mass, binding energy and radius have been determined.
tldr: This paper studies exciton properties in bulk 2H-MoTe2 using electron energy-loss spectroscopy and optical absorption, focusing on anisotropic effective masses and binding energy.
motivation: Understanding exciton behavior in transition metal dichalcogenides is important for optoelectronic applications, but this work is purely a materials characterization study.
method: The authors combine electron energy-loss spectroscopy in transmission and optical absorption spectroscopy to measure exciton dispersion along ΓK and ΓM directions at 20 K, extracting effective masses and binding parameters.
result: The exciton effective mass is found to be anisotropic, and the reduced mass, binding energy, and radius are determined from complementary optical data.
conclusion: The study provides detailed exciton parameters for 2H-MoTe2, but it does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Low-dimensional Dynamical Behavior Of Locally Coupled Chiral Swarmalators
authors: Zihan Li, Yonggang Wu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Zhigang Zheng And Duxin Chen
abstract: Understanding the dynamical behavior of swarmalators, particularly the transition from disorder to synchronization, constitutes one of the pivotal frontiers in the study of complex systems. We propose an ansatz that successfully decouples the spatial and phase dynamics in the locally coupled chiral swarmalators model, enabling rigorous analytical treatment of this complex system. Within this framework, we systematically examine how the interaction radius affects system synchronization, quantified through an order parameter measuring phase coherence. Our theoretical analysis reveals that increasing the interaction radius enhances synchronization in both velocity and phase dynamics. This relationship demonstrates that larger interaction networks facilitate more efficient information transfer among heterogeneous oscillators with different intrinsic frequencies. Using a self-consistent approach in the thermodynamic limit, we derive analytical expressions for the order parameter that accurately predict the synchronization transition. These findings provide fundamental insights into synchronization mechanisms in spatially embedded swarmalator systems with applications in understanding biological collective behaviors.
tldr: This paper analyzes synchronization in a model of chiral swarmalators with local coupling, deriving analytical expressions for the order parameter.
motivation: Understanding synchronization in swarmalator systems is important for biological collective behaviors, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors propose an ansatz to decouple spatial and phase dynamics, then use a self-consistent approach in the thermodynamic limit to derive analytical expressions for the order parameter.
result: They find that increasing the interaction radius enhances synchronization in both velocity and phase dynamics, and their analytical predictions match the synchronization transition.
conclusion: The work provides insights into synchronization mechanisms in spatially embedded swarmalator systems, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

title: Competing Magnetic Order In EuPd 3 ...
authors: Michelle Ocker, Franziska Walther, Nour Maraytta, Matthieu Le Tacon, Michael Merz, Cornelius Krellner And Kristin Kliemt
abstract: Single crystals of EuPd Si were grown using a high-temperature EuPd-flux method. The material was structurally and chemically characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction, powder x-ray diffraction, Laue method and energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. The structural analysis confirmed the orthorhombic crystal structure (space group ) but revealed differences in the lattice parameters and bond distances. The composition is close to the ideal 1:3:2 stoichiometry with an occupation of 7% of the Si sites by Pd. The heat capacity, electrical resistivity, and magnetic susceptibility show two magnetic transitions indicating magnetic ordering below 61 K and a spin reorientation at 40 K. The orthorhombic material shows magnetic anisotropy, with anisotropy constants and , for field applied along the three main symmetry axes, which is summarized in the temperature-field phase diagrams. The susceptibility data hint to an alignment of the magnetic moments along between and . Below the magnetic structure changes to an arrangement with moments canted away from . The single crystals investigated in this study are suggested to show antiferromagnetic order below instead of ferromagnetism that sets in at higher which might originate from certain differences in the structure, composition or defects that have an impact on the dominant coupling constants of the Ruderman–Kittel–Kasuya–Yosida interaction.
tldr: This paper reports the synthesis and characterization of EuPd3Si2 single crystals, focusing on their structural and magnetic properties.
motivation: The study aims to understand the magnetic ordering and anisotropy in EuPd3Si2, which may be relevant for fundamental physics but not directly tied to the user's research interests.
method: Single crystals were grown using a flux method and characterized via X-ray diffraction, EDX, heat capacity, resistivity, and magnetic susceptibility measurements.
result: Two magnetic transitions were observed at 61 K and 40 K, with anisotropic magnetic behavior and a spin reorientation, suggesting antiferromagnetic order below 61 K.
conclusion: The material exhibits complex magnetic behavior influenced by structural details, but the work is primarily condensed matter physics without a clear quantum information or thermodynamics angle.

title: A Study Of The Dimer-trimer Crossover In A Driven Three-component Fermi Gas
authors: R Slowinski, G Servignat, F Chevy And C Lobo
abstract: We develop an effective field theory for a system with three distinguishable atomic species and present a variational calculation of the two and three-body binding energies in vacuum and in the presence of a single Fermi sea. Specifically, we consider the case where the interaction between first two atomic species is externally driven so as to produce a (non-universal) closed-channel dimer whose coupling can be controlled independently of all other interactions. We then model the remaining interactions as a contact interaction between the dimer and a third atomic species which forms the medium. We derive analytical expressions for the dimer and trimer binding energies in vacuum and in medium, and in the latter case we predict a crossing between the dimer and trimer branches as a function of the atom–dimer scattering length, analogous to the usual polaron and molecule problem. Furthermore, we show that the position of this crossing can be controlled by varying the atom–atom coupling that results from the external drive and we discuss the implications of these findings.
tldr: This paper develops an effective field theory for a driven three-component Fermi gas, studying dimer-trimer crossover in vacuum and in a Fermi sea.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the crossover between dimer and trimer states in a driven Fermi gas, which is relevant to ultracold atomic physics and few-body physics.
method: They use an effective field theory with a variational calculation to compute two- and three-body binding energies, modeling the driven interaction as a closed-channel dimer and the remaining interactions as contact interactions.
result: They derive analytical expressions for dimer and trimer binding energies and predict a crossing between the dimer and trimer branches as a function of atom-dimer scattering length, controllable by the external drive.
conclusion: The findings have implications for controlling few-body states in driven Fermi gases, but the topic is far from the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Bridging Scales: From Classical Colloidal Crystals To Mesocrystals With Modern X-ray Synchrotron Methods
authors: Janne-Mieke Meijer, Elena V Sturm, Andrei V Petukhov And Ivan A Vartanyants
abstract: This review explores different colloidal systems and their crystals as well as their special case namely—mesocrystals. First, we highlight recent advances in fabrication methods of colloidal crystals (mesocrystals) and then describe small-angle and ultra-small-angle x-ray scattering from colloidal assemblies organized from particles of different shape. Here, we already introduce different types of defects that are present in colloidal crystals. Next, we go to a modern description of angular x-ray cross-correlation analysis and its applications on colloidal and mesocrystalline materials. After that we discuss phase retrieval techniques, namely coherent x-ray diffraction imaging and ptychography, as emerging tools for structural characterization of colloidal crystals and mesocrystals. We conclude with perspectives on the opportunities that will be provided by the 4th generation synchrotron sources for studying colloidal crystals and mesocrystals.
tldr: This review covers colloidal crystals and mesocrystals, focusing on X-ray scattering and imaging techniques, which are not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to review recent advances in fabricating and characterizing colloidal crystals and mesocrystals using modern synchrotron X-ray methods.
method: It reviews small-angle and ultra-small-angle X-ray scattering, angular X-ray cross-correlation analysis, and coherent X-ray diffraction imaging and ptychography.
result: The review highlights the capabilities of these techniques for structural characterization and discusses future opportunities with 4th generation synchrotron sources.
conclusion: The paper concludes that modern X-ray methods provide powerful tools for studying colloidal crystals and mesocrystals, with promising prospects for future research.

title: Review For Stokes-vector And Mueller-matrix Polarization Imaging Technology: Principles, Implementation And Applications
authors: Nan Wang, Houxin Fan, Quanzhou Long And Sailing He
abstract: This review systematically summarizes the principles, technological advancements, and diverse applications of Stokes-vector and Mueller-matrix polarization imaging (PI). The polarization of light is a fundamental property that provides unique and valuable information about the interaction between light and matter. While traditional polarimetry is limited to point-by-point measurements, PI captures the polarization state in a two-dimensional scene, generating a spatial map of parameters for complex and heterogeneous systems. The Stokes–Mueller formalism is the only complete mathematical tool for polarization analysis, using the Stokes vector to describe the light’s state and the Mueller matrix as the transfer function to fully characterize the polarization-altering properties of any medium, including complex depolarizing tissues. The evolution of PI from time-sequential to snapshot paradigms represents a pivotal shift, driven by the pressing need for real-time, motion-artifact-free characterization of dynamic systems. While time-sequential systems laid the foundational framework, their inherent trade-off between acquisition speed and polarization completeness has spurred intense innovation in snapshot methodologies. This transition is not merely a technical improvement but a fundamental enabler for applying polarization analysis to in vivo biological processes and real-time industrial inspection. Applications of PI are wide-ranging, including label-free diagnostics for cancer detection, non-destructive analysis of anisotropic materials, polarization-enhanced target detection, and so on. A future direction is the convergence of PI with hyperspectral detection to form ‘hyper-Stokes/Mueller imaging,’ which promises unprecedented specificity and real-time capability.
tldr: This paper is a review of Stokes-vector and Mueller-matrix polarization imaging technology, covering principles, implementations, and applications.
motivation: The authors aim to systematically summarize the state of the art in polarization imaging, which is a powerful tool for label-free diagnostics and material characterization.
method: The review synthesizes the mathematical formalism (Stokes-Mueller), discusses the evolution from time-sequential to snapshot imaging, and surveys various applications.
result: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of polarization imaging techniques and highlights future directions such as hyper-Stokes/Mueller imaging.
conclusion: Polarization imaging is a mature yet evolving field with broad applications, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Paradox Of Steady-state Light Diffusion
authors: André Liemert, Lorenzo Pattelli, Alwin Kienle, Federico Tommasi And Fabrizio Martelli
abstract: For over thirty years, the definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been the subject of persistent debate. Its canonical expression includes an explicit dependence on absorption, violating a fundamental scaling property of the radiative transfer equation (RTE). In the time domain (TD), evidence shows that the correct definition is independent of absorption, yet absorption-dependent formulations unfortunately remain common in practical data analysis. In the continuous-wave regime, the radial decay of the RTE can be reproduced by an absorption-dependent coefficient, but this does not imply that steady-state transport is genuinely diffusive. Here, this controversy is resolved through an exact consistency test based solely on the requirement that diffusion converges to the RTE in the limit of infinite propagation. In the TD, we prove that the absorption-independent coefficient is both necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence. In the continuous-wave regime, we prove analytically that no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE when absorption is nonzero: matching the dominant attenuation length fixes one coefficient, whereas matching the residue requires a different one. We further show that this failure is not caused by any finite set of ballistic or few-scattering contributions, and quantify the intrinsic error introduced by incorrect parameterizations in idealized absorption-retrieval scenarios. These results establish the time-domain formulation as the only self-consistent reference and call for a re-examination of how diffusion is applied in optical transport studies.
tldr: This paper resolves the long-standing debate on the definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport, proving that in steady-state with absorption no scalar diffusion coefficient can asymptotically match the radiative transfer equation.
motivation: The definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been debated for decades, with absorption-dependent formulations violating scaling properties of the RTE. The authors aim to resolve this controversy through an exact consistency test.
method: The authors use analytical proofs based on the requirement that diffusion converges to the RTE in the limit of infinite propagation, analyzing both time-domain and continuous-wave regimes.
result: In the time domain, the absorption-independent coefficient is necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence. In the continuous-wave regime, no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE when absorption is nonzero.
conclusion: The time-domain formulation is the only self-consistent reference, and the paper calls for re-examining diffusion applications in optical transport studies.

title: Emergent Symmetry-protected Topological Phases Via Polyakov Confinement In Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Shun-Li Yu And Jian-Xin Li Li-Wei He
abstract: A main theme in modern condensed matter physics is the emergence of fractionalized excitations and gauge structures from quantum spin systems. However, understanding how these exotic degrees of freedom reconfine into new phases of matter remains a fundamental challenge. In this work, we demonstrate that Polyakov’s confinement mechanism-a foundation of compact gauge theory-can serve as a dynamical engine to transform a Dirac spin liquid (DSL) into a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) state. Starting with a DSL with spin-dependent gauge fluxes, we show that the single-occupancy constraint inherent to the physical Hilbert space triggers monopole condensation, dynamically confining bulk spinons while preserving gapless edge modes-realizing a spinon analog of the quantum spin Hall effect. Using a large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulation on a triangular antiferromagnet with an additional Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, we provide microscopic evidence for this confined SPT phase, including a characteristic area law for the Wilson loop and vanishing topological entanglement entropy. Furthermore, we identify a measurable spin-pump response under magnetic fields, which directly encodes the Berry curvature of the parent Dirac cones. Our results reveal a previously unexplored pathway to SPT physics, bridging the fields of gauge theory, quantum magnetism, and topological matter.
tldr: This paper uses Polyakov confinement to transform a Dirac spin liquid into a symmetry-protected topological state in a quantum spin system, with numerical evidence from variational Monte Carlo.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how fractionalized excitations and gauge structures in quantum spin systems can reconfine into new phases of matter, specifically exploring a mechanism to generate SPT phases.
method: They employ large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulations on a triangular antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, analyzing Wilson loops and topological entanglement entropy.
result: They find evidence for a confined SPT phase with gapless edge modes, area-law Wilson loop, and vanishing topological entanglement entropy, and identify a spin-pump response.
conclusion: The work reveals a new pathway to SPT physics via Polyakov confinement, bridging gauge theory, quantum magnetism, and topological matter.

title: Tailoring Reflectionless Complex Media For non-Abelian Braiding Of Acoustic Modes
authors: Hongkuan Zhang And Guancong Ma
abstract: Multiple scattering of sound and light can be tailored for diverse applications. Despite the great progress enabled by technologies such as time-reversal propagation and wavefront shaping, the full control of the transmission matrix remains a significant challenge. In this work, we propose a multi-scattering-based approach to design reflectionless complex media with an arbitrary unitary transmission matrix. As such, the perfect transmission of waves through such a medium performs a unitary operation. Based on this principle, we experimentally demonstrated braiding of multiple waveguide modes in an acoustic waveguide via multiple scattering and showed non-Abelian characteristics arising from the concatenation of distinct complex media. Furthermore, we show that the principle can be extended for realizing arbitrary unitary operations beyond braiding. Our scheme uses generalized Wigner–Smith operators to design the optimal acoustic complex media with near-arbitrary targeted functionalities. The scheme is generally applicable beyond acoustics, with broad implications to other wave types. Our results demonstrate unprecedented control over multiple-scattering waves and establish complex media as a viable route to modal control and operations on compact platforms, providing a new design paradigm for multimode, reconfigurable wave-based devices with potential applications in multiplexed communication, imaging, and the manipulation of quantum waves.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to design reflectionless complex media with arbitrary unitary transmission matrices, experimentally demonstrating non-Abelian braiding of acoustic waveguide modes.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve full control of the transmission matrix in complex media, which is a significant challenge, and to explore non-Abelian operations for wave-based devices.
method: They use generalized Wigner-Smith operators to design acoustic complex media that achieve targeted unitary transmission matrices, and experimentally implement braiding of multiple waveguide modes.
result: They experimentally demonstrated non-Abelian braiding of acoustic modes and showed that the principle can be extended to arbitrary unitary operations.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new paradigm for multimode, reconfigurable wave-based devices with potential applications in communication, imaging, and quantum wave manipulation, but it is not directly aligned with the user's research interests.

title: Moiré-driven Skyrmion Family
authors: Kuan He, Meng-Han Li, Shi-Da Fan, Zi-Bin Lin, Xiao-Ying Zhuang, Cheng-Lin Han, Li-Qun Chen, Zhao-Dong Xu, Xue-Feng Zhu And Tian-Zhi Yang
abstract: Skyrmion family members, including skyrmions, merons, and skyrmioniums, have been observed in diverse physical systems, yet their coexistence and transformation within a single controllable platform remain challenging. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system that enables the generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges. By constructing three-dimensional displacement vector fields, we establish a framework describing the evolution of topological invariants under twist-induced symmetry modulation, thereby governing controlled transitions and the stable coexistence of different skyrmion textures. In addition, manipulating the Lamb-wave phase introduces discontinuous transport of the topological textures, thereby revealing phason-like dynamics within the quasiperiodic structure. Together, these results provide a versatile route for controlling topological textures and open new possibilities for the design of integrated topological wave devices.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a moiré-driven elastic system that generates and controls skyrmion family members, focusing on topological textures in mechanical metamaterials.
motivation: The authors aim to achieve coexistence and transformation of multiple skyrmion family members in a single controllable platform, which has been challenging in diverse physical systems.
method: They construct a bilayer twisted moiré elastic system and use three-dimensional displacement vector fields to describe topological invariants under twist-induced symmetry modulation, also manipulating Lamb-wave phase for discontinuous transport.
result: They experimentally demonstrate generation of multiple skyrmion family members with different topological charges and controlled transitions, revealing phason-like dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a versatile route for controlling topological textures and opens possibilities for integrated topological wave devices.

title: Probing Quark Electromagnetic Properties Via Entangled Quark Pairs In Fragmentation Hadrons At Lepton Colliders
authors: Qing-Hong Cao, Guanghui Li, Xin-Kai Wen And Bin Yan
abstract: Electromagnetic dipole interactions of light quarks induce distinct spin correlations in quark pairs produced at lepton colliders, favoring entangled spin-triplet state aligned along the axis or spin-singlet state. These correlations lead to unique azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive -dihadron pair production and in back-to-back hadron pairs ( ), which are absent in the SM. Using published Belle and BaBar measurements together with projected sensitivities based on ratios of azimuthal asymmetries, we demonstrate that these measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings, with a reduced dependence on poorly known nonperturbative fragmentation functions and free from contamination by other new physics effects. This approach offers a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes using spin correlations in entangled quark pairs produced at lepton colliders to probe light-quark electromagnetic dipole moments, analyzing azimuthal asymmetries in hadron pair production.
motivation: To constrain light-quark dipole couplings, which are poorly known and could indicate new physics, using a clean collider observable.
method: The authors derive spin correlations from dipole interactions, predict azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive dihadron and back-to-back hadron pair production, and use Belle/BaBar data plus projected sensitivities to constrain the couplings.
result: The proposed measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings with reduced dependence on fragmentation functions and no contamination from other new physics.
conclusion: This offers a novel and clean probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.

title: El Agente Cuántico: Automating Quantum Simulations
authors: Ignacio Gustin, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Juan B Pérez-Sánchez, Chris Crebolder, Jérôme F Gonthier, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Yuma Nakamura, Karthik Panicker, Manav Ramprasad, Aiwei Yin, Zijian Zhang, Yunheng Zou, Varinia Bernales And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract: Quantum simulation is central to understanding and designing quantum systems across physics and chemistry. However, its practical use is often limited by the exponential growth of Hilbert space and by the increasing complexity of modern quantum-simulation software. Here we introduce El Agente Cuántico, a multi-agent AI system that automates quantum-simulation workflows by translating natural-language scientific intent into executed and validated computations across heterogeneous quantum-software frameworks. By reasoning directly over library documentation and APIs, our agentic system dynamically assembles end-to-end simulations spanning—but not limited to—state preparation, closed- and open-system dynamics, tensor-network methods, quantum control, quantum error correction, and quantum resource estimation. The developed system unifies traditionally distinct simulation paradigms behind a single natural-language interface. Beyond reducing technical barriers, this approach opens a path toward scalable, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous quantum simulation, enabling faster exploration of physical models, rapid hypothesis testing, and closer integration between theory, simulation, and emerging quantum hardware.
tldr: This paper introduces an AI agent system that automates quantum simulation workflows via natural language, but it does not directly contribute to the core research directions.
motivation: Quantum simulation is limited by complexity and software fragmentation; the authors aim to lower barriers and accelerate research.
method: They develop a multi-agent AI system that interprets natural language, reasons over documentation and APIs, and assembles end-to-end simulations across various quantum software frameworks.
result: The system unifies different simulation paradigms behind a single interface, enabling automated state preparation, dynamics, tensor networks, control, error correction, and resource estimation.
conclusion: This approach could make quantum simulation more accessible and adaptive, but it is more about software automation than advancing fundamental quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: From Intuition To Optimization: A Review Of Inverse Design Applied To Optical Nanotweezers
authors: Sejeong Kim And Kenneth B Crozier Damian Nelson
abstract: Optical nanotweezers, which integrate nanophotonic structures such as plasmonic antennas, dielectric resonators, and metasurfaces, have emerged as powerful tools for manipulating nanoparticles, biomolecules, and viruses with high precision. However, traditional designs rely heavily on heuristic approaches and simple geometries, limiting performance. Inverse design offers a paradigm shift by using computational optimization methods to discover non-intuitive, high-performance structures for optical trapping. This review provides an overview of key inverse design methodologies, including adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning approaches, and highlights their broader impact across nanophotonics. We then focus on their application to optical nanotweezers, where recent advances demonstrate enhanced trapping stiffness, reduced optical heating, and tailored trapping landscapes. Representative examples include algorithmic design of plasmonic nanotweezers, topology-optimized plasmonic nanoapertures, inverse-designed dielectric nanocavities, and force-centric designs based on Maxwell stress tensor engineering. Collectively, these studies illustrate how inverse design enables stable, efficient, and versatile optical trapping at the nanoscale. Despite these advances, challenges remain in fabrication, computational cost, and the interpretability of optimized structures. We conclude with a perspective on future directions, emphasizing opportunities in reconfigurable tweezers, lab-on-a-chip integration, and quantum nanophotonics. By bridging photonic optimization with nanoscale manipulation, inverse-designed optical nanotweezers offer promising opportunities for future applications in biophysics, materials science, and quantum technologies.
tldr: This review covers inverse design methods for optical nanotweezers, focusing on nanophotonics and optical trapping, with only a brief mention of quantum nanophotonics.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize recent advances in inverse design for optical nanotweezers, which are used for manipulating nanoparticles and biomolecules, and to highlight challenges and future directions.
method: The review discusses adjoint-based optimization, topology optimization, and machine learning approaches, and provides examples of their application to optical nanotweezers.
result: Inverse design enhances trapping stiffness, reduces heating, and enables tailored trapping landscapes, but faces challenges in fabrication, computational cost, and interpretability.
conclusion: Inverse-designed optical nanotweezers have potential in biophysics, materials science, and quantum technologies, but further development is needed.

tldr: This paper proposes a method to approximate hyperedges in higher-order networks to model stochastic processes like cooperation and opinion dynamics.
motivation: Most theories of social dynamics assume pairwise interactions, but many real-world interactions are higher-order (e.g., collaborations, public goods). The authors aim to capture these higher-order effects in stochastic process models.
method: They introduce a hyperedge approximation technique that simplifies higher-order network structures while preserving key dynamical features, likely using moment closure or mean-field approximations.
result: The approximation enables efficient simulation and analysis of stochastic processes on higher-order networks, with improved accuracy over pairwise models.
conclusion: The method provides a practical way to incorporate higher-order interactions into models of social and biological dynamics, with potential applications in evolutionary game theory and opinion dynamics.

title: Two-Stage Deformable-Convolutional Inverse Design Of Nanophotonic Absorbers From Optical Spectra
authors: Waleed Waseer, Muhammad Shahid Jabbar, Muhammad Sohail Ibrahim, Shujaat Khan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data-driven inverse design enables efficient generation of nanophotonic structures with prescribed optical responses, but spectrum-to-geometry mapping remains challenging due to non-uniqueness and fine geometric features. This work presents a two-stage deformable-convolutional framework for reconstructing metal--insulator--metal resonator geometries from 80-dimensional absorption spectra. The spectrum is projected to a [MATH] latent representation and decoded into a [MATH] resonator mask. Training combines supervised reconstruction with least-squares adversarial refinement initialized from the best supervised checkpoint. A three-run ablation compares deformable convolution with plain convolution, involution, Dynamic Conv, and ODConv under the same architecture. The proposed model achieves [MATH]~dB PSNR and [MATH] SSIM, improving over plain convolution by 2.16~dB and 0.0831, respectively. It further achieves Dice [MATH], IoU [MATH], and boundary F-score [MATH]. Spectral consistency evaluated using a frozen forward surrogate yields RMSE [MATH] and [MATH]. Learned offsets show stronger adaptive sampling at coarse and intermediate decoder stages. Overall, deformable sampling with supervised initialization and adversarial refinement improves spectrum-conditioned geometry reconstruction.
tldr: This paper presents a two-stage deformable-convolutional neural network for inverse design of nanophotonic absorbers from optical spectra, focusing on spectrum-to-geometry mapping.
motivation: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing nanophotonic structures from optical spectra, which is important for efficient design of photonic devices.
method: The method uses a two-stage framework: first, a supervised reconstruction of the resonator mask from the spectrum, then adversarial refinement. It compares deformable convolution with other convolution variants.
result: The proposed model achieves improved PSNR, SSIM, Dice, IoU, and boundary F-score compared to plain convolution, with better spectral consistency.
conclusion: Deformable sampling with supervised initialization and adversarial refinement improves spectrum-conditioned geometry reconstruction for nanophotonic absorbers.

title: Power Stability Of Finitely Generated Dynamical Frames For Positive Operators
authors: Jian Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \( \Lambda=\{\lambda_j\}_{j\in\mathbb N}\subset[0,1) \) be a finite union of Carleson sequences, and let \( \Lambda^p=\{\lambda_j^p\}_{j\in\mathbb N} \) for \(p>0\). We prove that \(\Lambda\) and \(\Lambda^p\) admit compatible Hartmann-type cluster decompositions and that, under the natural coordinate identification, \( H^2(\Lambda)=H^2(\Lambda^p). \) After taking account of the change in the normalization weights, this trace-space identity gives \( (T_\Lambda) = (T_{\Lambda^p}) \) for the associated weighted evaluation operators. The characterization of finitely generated dynamical frames for normal operators then implies that, for every positive operator \(A\in\mathcal B(H)\), every finite index set \(I\), and every \(p>0\), \( \{A^nf_i\}_{n\in\mathbb N,\,i\in I} H\) if and only if \( \{A^{pn}f_i\}_{n\in\mathbb N,\,i\in I} H. \) In particular, for every \(q\in\mathbb N^+\), the subfamily \( \{A^{qn}f_i\}_{n\in\mathbb N,\,i\in I} \) is still a frame, and hence every such dynamical frame has infinite excess. An example shows that the positivity assumption cannot in general be replaced by normality.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical frames for positive operators, proving that frame properties are invariant under powering the operator, but it is purely mathematical with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to characterize finitely generated dynamical frames for positive operators, extending known results to a broader class of operators.
method: The author uses Carleson sequences and Hartmann-type cluster decompositions to establish trace-space identities, then applies a characterization of dynamical frames for normal operators.
result: It is shown that for any positive operator A, the frame property of {A^n f_i} is equivalent to that of {A^{pn} f_i} for any p>0, and that such frames have infinite excess.
conclusion: The results are purely functional-analytic and do not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems, thus falling outside the user's research interests.

title: A Comparison Of Malware Image Transformations Using Grad-CAM And Hybrid Learning Models
authors: Mark Stamp Vibha Bhavikatti
abstract: ArXiv:2608.12077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent studies have shown that binary-to-image representations can enable effective machine learning-based results for malware detection and classification. However, performance can vary significantly, depending on the technique used to convert binaries to images. Furthermore, the explainability and interpretability of image-based models is largely unexplored within the malware domain. In this research, we employ Gradient-weighted Class Activation Maps (Grad-CAM) as an eXplainable AI (XAI) tool, which we use to analyze eight distinct image types derived from malware samples. We provide quantitative faithfulness and stability metrics for Grad-CAM heatmaps and we compare these heatmaps to High-Resolution Class Activation Mappings (HiResCAM). We also show that Grad-CAM heatmaps can provide useful information for malware classification. Specifically, we show that a Random Forest model trained on features extracted from Grad-CAM images via a MobileNetV2 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model achieves a test accuracy of 0.777 across 17 malware families, exceeding a previous benchmark of 0.750 for this same dataset. A key finding of this research is that for the malware image transformations considered, accuracy and explanation faithfulness do not coincide, e.g., image transformation techniques that produce the most faithful explanations yield only mid-tier accuracy.
tldr: This paper applies Grad-CAM and hybrid learning models to malware image transformations for classification, focusing on explainability and accuracy.
motivation: The authors aim to improve malware detection using image-based representations and to explore explainability of these models, which is largely unexplored in the malware domain.
method: They use Grad-CAM and HiResCAM to analyze eight image types from malware samples, extract features with MobileNetV2, and train a Random Forest classifier on Grad-CAM features.
result: The Random Forest model achieves 0.777 test accuracy across 17 malware families, exceeding a previous benchmark of 0.750, and they find that explanation faithfulness does not coincide with accuracy.
conclusion: The study demonstrates that Grad-CAM can provide useful explanations for malware classification, but the trade-off between faithfulness and accuracy suggests careful selection of image transformations.

title: Local Verification Cannot Detect Non-transportability: A Cohomological Theory Of Context Preservation In Agentic Reasoning
authors: Suyash Mishra
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic AI systems routinely transport conclusions across biological, clinical and financial contexts, and the emerging safeguard is local verification: checking at each step that the entity is representable in the chosen tool, that parameters are compatible, and that outputs cohere with the plan. We prove this class of safeguard is structurally incomplete. Modelling a covering of context space by its nerve and evidence by a real-valued 1-cochain, an agent chaining evidence performs path integration: its conclusion is path-independent if and only if the cochain is exact, and disagreement between valid reasoning paths is exactly the holonomy of a first Cech cohomology class. Hodge decomposition partitions evidence conflict into a gradient part (calibration), a curl part (local inconsistency, visible at triple overlaps) and a harmonic part. Our central result is that no family of simplex-supported consistency checks can distinguish omega from omega+h for harmonic h, which nonetheless generates non-zero disagreement between valid paths; detection requires a statistic on a cycle basis. The resulting procedure, Ksetra, estimates by coboundary projection and gates abstention on the harmonic component, which we give a mechanism: it arises from effect modification combined with overlap-specific population composition, and vanishes to machine precision when effect modification is absent. The degrees of freedom of an evidence network partition into calibration, coherence and transport, yielding an exact F-test for the existence of a global claim; we quantify its distortion under unequal precision and supply the precision-whitened form that restores exactness. Foreign exchange, where the arbitrage-free null makes the cochain exactly a coboundary, serves as a calibration bench: the test is correctly sized, fires on loop arbitrage, and ignores triangular arbitrage.
tldr: This paper applies cohomology and Hodge decomposition to analyze context preservation in agentic AI systems, proving that local verification cannot detect non-transportability.
motivation: The paper addresses a fundamental limitation in AI safety: local verification of agentic reasoning is insufficient to ensure global consistency when transporting conclusions across contexts.
method: The authors model context space as a nerve covering, evidence as a 1-cochain, and use path integration to relate path-independence to exactness. They apply Hodge decomposition to separate calibration, coherence, and transport, and propose a statistic on cycle basis to detect harmonic components.
result: They prove that no simplex-supported consistency checks can distinguish exact cochains from those differing by a harmonic component, which causes non-zero disagreement between valid reasoning paths. They introduce Ksetra, a procedure that estimates via coboundary projection and gates abstention on the harmonic component, and validate it on foreign exchange data.
conclusion: The paper establishes that local verification is structurally incomplete and proposes a cohomological framework to detect non-transportability, with implications for AI safety and reasoning validation.

title: Dimensionality And Confinement Reshape Competition In Cellular Renewing Active Matter
authors: Philip Bittihn And Yoav G Pollack Patrick Zimmer
abstract: Cellular renewing active matter—assemblies of proliferating and apoptotic cells—underlies tissue homeostasis, morphogenesis, and clonal competition. Previous work in one-dimensional periodic systems identified a fitness advantage associated with rapid dead-cell clearance, an ‘opportunistic’ competition mechanism. Extending this framework, we study two-dimensional cellular aggregates and show that dimensionality modifies the interplay between competition mechanisms for clones with different clearance rates: in 2D, opportunistic and homeostatic-pressure-based competition jointly shape clonal selection, to varying degrees. We then introduce an explicit circular confinement to probe how physical boundaries modulate this interplay. While opportunistic competition persists, distinct time-dependent behaviors emerge through weakened homeostatic-pressure-based competition near boundaries. Structural analysis reveals that confinement promotes tangential alignment and spatially heterogeneous homeostatic pressure, thereby reshaping competitive outcomes at tissue edges. Partial information decomposition allows us to attribute these differing outcomes to temporally and spatially varying relative contributions of the two mechanisms. Our study connects newly discovered competition mechanisms with more realistic biological contexts, highlighting how dimensionality and spatial constraints influence tissue structures and modulate competition in heterogeneous cell populations across time and space, with implications for tumor growth dynamics and tissue development.
tldr: This paper studies cellular renewing active matter in 2D with confinement, focusing on clonal competition mechanisms, which is outside the user's research interests.
motivation: To understand how dimensionality and spatial constraints affect competition in cellular aggregates, with implications for tissue development and tumor growth.
method: Extends a 1D model to 2D, introduces circular confinement, and uses partial information decomposition to analyze competition mechanisms.
result: Dimensionality and confinement alter the interplay between opportunistic and homeostatic-pressure-based competition, with boundary effects leading to heterogeneous pressure and tangential alignment.
conclusion: The findings highlight the importance of spatial constraints in shaping clonal selection, but the topic is not aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Compact Actively-Shielded Magnetic Field Coil Within Mu-Metal Shields For Acme Electric Dipole Moment Measurements
authors: S. Liu, M. Watts, C. Diver, D. G. Ang, C. Meisenhelder, X. Fan, B. Hao, D. Lascar, A. Hiramoto, T. Masuda, P. Hu, Z. Han, X. Wu, D. Demille, J. M. Doyle, G. Gabrielse
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A system of actively-shielded coils and mu-metal shields is devised, constructed and shown to provide the stable and spatially uniform magnetic field needed for the ACME III electron electric dipole moment (eEDM) measurement. Two layers of current-carrying coils, enclosed within three layers of ferromagnetic shields, produce a field that varies by less than 1 nT (10 [MATH]) within the 1 m [MATH] 4.2 cm [MATH] 4.2 cm interior volume in which a beam of ThO molecules are probed as they precess. The demountable shields are constructed from rectangular mu-metal plates. The largest, with a mass of 19 kg and an area of 2.18 m [MATH] 0.75 m, is easily carried by two people and just fits within a large available annealing oven. The assembly design facilitates low-stress mounting and handling to suppress changes in the magnetic properties of the mu metal, and also provides modular access to apparatus within the coils for maintenance and upgrades. The nearly static external ambient field is reduced within the shielded precession volume by up to a factor of [MATH]. During the magnetic field reversals that ACME uses to suppress systematic uncertainties, the ``actively-shielded'' coil largely cancels out its external fringing field to minimize the magnetization of the mu metal. Even though the shields are only 10 cm outside the coils, shield degaussing after every magnetic field reversal is not required. The non-reversing residual field stays below 1 nT for up to 17 hours when the field is reversed every 30 seconds, for example. The measured performance, compared to the previous generation ACME II apparatus, suggests that the magnetic-field-related systematic uncertainties for ACME III will be smaller by an estimated factor of 40 despite a five times longer precession volume and the use of three magnetic shielding layers rather than five.
tldr: This paper describes the engineering of a magnetic field coil system for an electron electric dipole moment measurement, which is not related to the user's research interests.
motivation: The ACME III experiment requires a highly stable and uniform magnetic field to measure the electron's electric dipole moment, which is a fundamental physics test. The paper aims to improve the magnetic field system to reduce systematic uncertainties.
method: The authors designed and constructed a system of actively-shielded coils enclosed in three layers of mu-metal shields, using demountable rectangular plates. They characterized the field uniformity and stability, and compared performance with the previous generation.
result: The system achieves field variation below 1 nT in the interior volume, reduces external ambient field by a large factor, and maintains non-reversing residual field below 1 nT for up to 17 hours. Estimated systematic uncertainties are reduced by a factor of 40 compared to ACME II.
conclusion: The new magnetic field system meets the stringent requirements for ACME III, demonstrating effective shielding and active cancellation, but the work is purely experimental physics unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ward Identities: A Geometric Point Of View And Applications
authors: Shengjing Xu Baojun Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The work of Baverez, Guillarmou, Kupiainen, and Rhodes [BGKR24] is the starting point of this paper. It shows that analytic changes of boundary parametrizations act differentiably on Liouville amplitudes, with derivative given by Virasoro operators and a scalar anomaly term. We compute this scalar term. Its holomorphic part is a Schwarzian boundary integral, which gives a geometric explanation of the Virasoro central term. We then derive local Ward identities on disks, annuli, and pairs of pants. They give finite recursions for descendant matrix coefficients. From these recursions we recover the polynomial factorization of normalized pair-of-pants coefficients. In the annular zero-weight limit, we recover the Shapovalov form. For a pair of pants with two incoming boundaries, we recover the formal chiral vertex-operator coefficients. We also give a geometric proof of smoothness in the bulk insertion points and derive the genus-zero arbitrary level BPZ equations for degenerate bulk insertions.
tldr: This paper derives Ward identities and geometric interpretations of Virasoro central terms in Liouville theory, focusing on conformal field theory and complex geometry.
motivation: The authors aim to compute a scalar anomaly term in Liouville amplitudes and provide geometric explanations for Virasoro central terms, extending prior work by Baverez et al.
method: They use analytic changes of boundary parametrizations, compute the scalar term as a Schwarzian boundary integral, and derive local Ward identities on disks, annuli, and pairs of pants.
result: They obtain finite recursions for descendant matrix coefficients, recover polynomial factorization of pair-of-pants coefficients, the Shapovalov form, and formal chiral vertex-operator coefficients, and prove smoothness in bulk insertion points.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric perspective on Ward identities and Virasoro central terms, with applications to conformal field theory and Liouville theory.

title: Towards Terabit/$\lambda$/s Multidimensional Silicon Photonic Engine
authors: Hao Chen, Zengqi Chen, Wu Zhou, Kaihang Lu, Mingyuan Zhang, Yuxiang Yin, Yiou Cui, Chaoran Huang, Pui-In Mak, Yeyu Tong
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Increasing artificial intelligence (AI) workloads drive co-packaged optics (CPO), which integrates optical engines with electronic components. Optical interconnects can extend transmission distances and reduce latency, allowing distributed clusters in AI factories to operate as a unified computational unit. However, escalating data throughput necessitates greater parallelization of light within ultracompact form factors while maintaining stringent energy efficiency and latency constraints. Here, we present a multidimensional silicon photonic engine that achieves a communication capacity exceeding 1.8 terabit/s/lambda/s. By monolithically integrating transceivers, spatial and polarization (de)multiplexers, and optical signal processors on a single chip, we eliminate bulky discrete (de)multiplexers and power-hungry digital signal processing (DSP). In experiments, the photonic engine can be self-configured to identify two, four, or six concurrent spatial and polarization channels per fiber while mitigating dynamic channel crosstalk. Compared with the state-of-art DSP, our approach achieves >5,000-fold reductions in both power consumption and processing latency at a MIMO processing order of six. Furthermore, we demonstrate full-duplex, modulation-format-transparent inter-chip communication over 300-meter fiber. These results represent a paradigm shift for optical engines in future high-performance computing and AI-driven data centers.
tldr: This paper presents a silicon photonic engine for co-packaged optics achieving >1.8 Tbps per wavelength, but it is primarily an applied photonics engineering result with no quantum information or thermodynamics content.
motivation: The paper aims to address the increasing data throughput demands in AI-driven data centers by integrating optical transceivers and multiplexers on a single chip to reduce power and latency.
method: The authors monolithically integrate transceivers, spatial and polarization multiplexers, and optical signal processors on a silicon chip, and demonstrate self-configuration for multiple channels with crosstalk mitigation.
result: The photonic engine achieves >1.8 Tbps per wavelength, with >5,000-fold reductions in power and latency compared to DSP, and demonstrates full-duplex inter-chip communication over 300 m fiber.
conclusion: The work represents a paradigm shift for optical engines in high-performance computing, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Near-Unity Excitation And Radiative Efficiencies In Electroluminescence Without External Carrier Injection
authors: Rui Li, Xinrui Li, Jiachen Xie, Pingjun Xu, Wen Li, Congcong Liu, Zheng Ge, Longjia Wu, Xingtong Chen, Zheming Liu, Song Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroluminescence occurring without external charge injection is typically characterized by weak emission and excessive driving voltage, due to low excitation and radiative recombination efficiencies. Here, we demonstrate non-injecting electroluminescence (NI-EL) that challenges this conventional perception. To achieve this, we introduce an operational paradigm that leverages remote, state-abundant charge reservoirs, which elevates the excitation efficiency close to unity - a greater-than-20-fold improvement over the benchmark. This strategy is augmented by quantum dots (QDs) with nonmonotonically graded shells, raising the high-field radiative efficiency by approximately 7-8-fold. The resultant RGB NI-EL devices uniformly exhibit bright and efficient pulsed emissions, with key metrics including: a turn-on threshold of 3.7 Vrms for red; a luminance of 291,628 nits and a power efficiency of 302.6 lm/W for green, with light-outcoupling enhancement; and, for blue, the superior emitter stability of the first QD-based blue NI-EL over its light-emitting diode counterpart. The minimal dielectric loss, sub-100 ns response time, and external EL efficiency of up to 45.4% further reinforce the mechanism-performance causality. These results overcome the inherent mechanistic limitations of NI-EL and establish performance that rivals or surpasses injection-type EL, including AC- or DC-driven variants, positioning NI-EL as a promising platform for high-performance pulsed light sources.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-efficiency electroluminescence without external carrier injection using quantum dots with graded shells, achieving near-unity excitation efficiency and high brightness.
motivation: Conventional non-injecting electroluminescence suffers from weak emission and high driving voltage; the authors aim to overcome these limitations to enable practical pulsed light sources.
method: They introduce an operational paradigm using remote charge reservoirs to boost excitation efficiency, and employ quantum dots with nonmonotonically graded shells to enhance radiative efficiency under high fields.
result: RGB NI-EL devices show bright and efficient pulsed emissions, with green achieving 291,628 nits and 302.6 lm/W, and external EL efficiency up to 45.4%.
conclusion: The results establish NI-EL as a promising platform for high-performance pulsed light sources, rivaling or surpassing injection-type EL.

title: A Uniform Elliptic Reduction, An Order-matching Criterion, And Precision Benchmarks For The Strong-coupling Birman-Schwinger Analysis Of The Lattice Three-boson Trimer
authors: Mikhail Dolgopolov
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the strong-coupling Birman-Schwinger analysis of the three-boson lattice Schroedinger operator at the exceptional quasimomentum K = pi. First, we provide an exact closed-form benchmark for the fiber Fredholm determinant at a distinguished flat momentum, valid for every quasimomentum K, obtained via a uniform elliptic reduction of the two-dimensional lattice integral. Second, we formulate and prove a general order-matching criterion. This criterion decides whether a leading-order Fredholm determinant asymptotic, with relative accuracy of order 1/mu, suffices to determine the constant-order additive correction in the strong-coupling energy, or if the next-order refinement is required. Applying the criterion at K = pi, we derive the complete strong-coupling ground-state asymptotics, including the coefficient of the order 1/mu term. The results are cross-validated against the exact closed-form benchmark and two independent high-precision numerical schemes. Furthermore, we determine the corresponding spectral gap and prove an exact Fredholm-determinant underestimation factor equal to 2. Additionally, we independently confirm that the previously established K = 0 constant is correctly derived and requires no analogous refinement. Finally, we compare the orders of asymptotic precision controlled across recent lattice few-body models and draw a structural parallel with the parity classification of topological band structures.
tldr: This paper presents a mathematical analysis of the strong-coupling Birman-Schwinger operator for a lattice three-boson trimer, focusing on asymptotic expansions and Fredholm determinants.
motivation: The paper aims to provide exact benchmarks and criteria for asymptotic expansions in the strong-coupling limit of a lattice three-boson system, which is a problem in mathematical physics.
method: The author uses uniform elliptic reduction of lattice integrals, formulates an order-matching criterion, and applies it to derive ground-state asymptotics, cross-validating with numerical schemes.
result: The paper derives complete strong-coupling ground-state asymptotics, including the order 1/mu term, and proves an exact Fredholm-determinant underestimation factor of 2.
conclusion: The results provide rigorous benchmarks and criteria for similar lattice few-body models, with a structural parallel to topological band structures.

title: A Unified Analytic Approach To O-metric Inequalities And Applications To Fixed Point Theory
authors: Hallowed Oluwadara Olaoluwa, Aminat Olawunmi Ige, Johnson Olajire Olaleru
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The concept of O-metrics was recently introduced as a generalization of several metric-type structures by replacing the addition operation of the standard triangle inequality with a binary operation that may fail to be associative. This non-associativity naturally to generalized polygon inequalities and patterned compositions. In this work we develop an analytic framework for inequalities arising in such settings. By introducing generalized [MATH]-series governed by admissible control functions [MATH], we establish a separation principle that resolves inequalities of the form [MATH]. This result provides convergence criteria for patterned compositions and determines intervals for the admissible contraction parameter [MATH]. As application, some fixed point theorems of \'{C}iri\'{c} type are obtained for mappings on O-metric spaces, as well as corresponding results for b-metric spaces. The approach provides a unified analytic framework for studying contractive conditions and iterative processes in generalized metric spaces.
tldr: This paper develops an analytic framework for inequalities in O-metric spaces, a generalization of metric spaces, and applies it to fixed point theory.
motivation: The paper aims to unify and extend results in generalized metric spaces by introducing a new analytic approach to handle non-associative triangle inequalities.
method: The authors introduce generalized series governed by admissible control functions and establish a separation principle to resolve inequalities, then apply it to prove fixed point theorems of Ciric type.
result: They obtain convergence criteria for patterned compositions and determine intervals for contraction parameters, leading to new fixed point theorems in O-metric and b-metric spaces.
conclusion: The work provides a unified analytic framework for contractive conditions in generalized metric spaces, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Combinatorial And Sampling Approaches To Determining The Priority Vector From An Incomplete Pairwise Comparison Matrix On The Set Of Spanning Trees
authors: Oksana Mulesa Vitaliy Tsyganok
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers combinatorial and sampling approaches to deriving a priority vector from an incomplete pairwise comparison matrix. It is shown that the informationally significant combinations of matrix elements are in one-to-one correspondence with spanning trees of the graph induced by the matrix. The combinatorial approach is based on the enumeration of all spanning trees and the componentwise aggregation of the priority vectors derived from them. To reduce computational complexity, a sampling Monte Carlo approach with a sequential stopping criterion is proposed, ensuring a prescribed accuracy for estimating the components of the resulting vector.
tldr: This paper proposes combinatorial and sampling methods to derive priority vectors from incomplete pairwise comparison matrices using spanning trees.
motivation: The authors aim to handle incomplete pairwise comparison matrices in decision-making, where traditional methods fail due to missing data.
method: They establish a one-to-one correspondence between informationally significant matrix element combinations and spanning trees, then aggregate priority vectors from all spanning trees. To reduce complexity, they introduce a Monte Carlo sampling approach with a sequential stopping criterion.
result: The combinatorial approach enumerates all spanning trees, while the sampling approach provides a computationally efficient alternative with guaranteed accuracy.
conclusion: The proposed methods offer a principled way to derive priority vectors from incomplete matrices, with the sampling approach balancing accuracy and computational cost.

title: Orthonormal Bases For Higher Hilbert Spaces
authors: Giovanni Ferrer, Brett Hungar, David Penneys, Greyson Wesley
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11358v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In our previous article [arxiv:2410.05120], we introduced the notion of a finite dimensional 3-Hilbert space, categorifying Baez's 2-Hilbert spaces. In this article, by further categorifying Baez's higher linear algebra, we provide useful tools for working with 3-Hilbert spaces, including, generalized scalar multiplication, orthonormal bases, and unitary adjoints for operators. title: Convex-Concave Interpolation And Application Of Pep To Bilinear-Coupled Saddle-Point Problem
authors: Valery Krivchenko, Alexander Gasnikov, Dmitry Kovalev
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Performance estimation problem (PEP) approach reformulates finding the exact worst-case performance of an algorithm as the solution to an optimization problem. Tractable formulation of the problem requires necessary and sufficient interpolation conditions. We present the interpolation conditions for convex--concave functions, bilinear functions, and composite functions with bilinear coupling. We also construct PEP for first-order methods for composite saddle-point problem.

title: Stability Of Finite-Batch Particle Mean-Field Variational Inference Beyond Strong Convexity
authors: Truong Vu Vinh Nguyen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11486v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the implementable finite-batch particle algorithm for mean-field variational inference as a fully discrete stochastic approximation of the projected Wasserstein dynamics. The target potential is globally smooth but need not be strongly convex. The departure from contractivity is quantified by the curvature defect \[ \mathfrak d_\alpha(x,y) = \bigl[\alpha\|x-y\|^2- \langle\nabla V(x)-\nabla V(y),x-y\rangle\bigr]_+, \] which is the additive loss in the one-step Euler contraction estimate. title: Pseudo-differential Operator Associated With The Linear Canonical Dunkl Transform

title: Sparse Rotatable Arrays (sra): Unifying Array Aperture And Antenna Directivity For Wireless Communications
authors: Ailing Zheng, Qingqing Wu, Xiyuan Liu, Wen Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse arrays reduce the hardware cost of extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output systems while preserving a large effective aperture, but may suffer from severe sidelobe and grating-lobe leakage. Rotatable antennas (RAs) provide directional leakage suppression, whereas frequent boresight adaptation to instantaneous user locations incurs considerable control overhead. In practice, long-term user distributions are often non-uniform, with compact hotspots coexisting with scattered users, which enables low-complexity RA configuration based on group-level geometry. Motivated by this observation, we propose a group-aware sparse RA architecture in which users are organized into service groups and the activated RAs are partitioned into group-specific sparse subarrays. We maximize the minimum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) among all users by jointly optimizing the sparse-aperture allocation, RA orientations, and transmit beamforming. We show that RA-induced inter-group leakage suppression and sparse-aperture-induced intra-group orthogonalization jointly yield an approximately decoupled group-wise beamforming structure, providing physical guidance for group-wise antenna-number allocation and non-periodic sparse-position initialization. Guided by these insights, we develop a structured low-complexity two-layer algorithm that embeds a closed-form projected group-center RA orientation rule into the sparse-aperture allocation and beamforming design. The algorithm combines analysis-guided initialization, sampled multi-start antenna-allocation search, and bisection-based second-order cone programming for beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed design closely approaches the fully shared and orientation-optimized benchmarks while substantially outperforming the compact and omnidirectional sparse-array schemes.

motivation: The paper addresses hardware cost and sidelobe leakage in massive MIMO systems by combining sparse arrays with rotatable antennas, aiming to reduce control overhead while maintaining performance.
method: The authors introduce a group-aware sparse RA architecture, jointly optimizing sparse-aperture allocation, RA orientations, and transmit beamforming via a low-complexity two-layer algorithm.
result: Numerical results show the proposed design closely approaches fully shared and orientation-optimized benchmarks, outperforming compact and omnidirectional sparse-array schemes.
conclusion: The proposed architecture offers a practical trade-off between hardware cost and performance for wireless communications, but it is not related to quantum information or quantum technologies.

title: Tight Nonasymptotic Local Convergence Of Sinkhorn-Knopp
authors: Wenzhi Gao, Zhaonan Qu, Yinyu Ye, Madeleine Odell
abstract: ArXiv:2608.11760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the Sinkhorn-Knopp (SK) algorithm for the matrix scaling problem. Despite extensive literature on the global convergence of SK and its variants, its local linear convergence behavior remains less understood.
